rows.title: Chicken Delight
rows.dek: A sweet and tangy family favorite from the American convenience-food kitchen, where a bottle and a packet did the seasoning. Dry onion soup mix arrived in 1952 and soon turned up in the famous California dip.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, cut up (breasts, legs and thighs)
steps: Put the chicken in a baking dish.
Mix the dressing, soup mix and jam.
Pour the sauce over the chicken.
Bake 1 hour at 350°F.
Serve with rice, with the extra sauce poured over the rice.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Raspberry jam works when there's no apricot.
rows.serve_with: Baked Rice and steamed green beans

rows.title: Melt in Your Mouth Chicken
rows.dek: A family favorite: baked chicken under a mayonnaise and parmesan crust, the kind of recipe Hellmann's prints as its Parmesan Crusted Chicken. It stays moist and golden every time.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Mix the parmesan, mayonnaise and seasonings.
Spread it over the chicken breasts.
Bake 45 minutes at 375°F.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.serve_with: Baked Rice and steamed broccoli

rows.title: Easy Oven Fried Chicken
rows.dek: A family favorite, the home-oven take on Southern fried chicken: dredged in seasoned flour, then baked in butter instead of fried in a deep pan of fat.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Melt the butter in a shallow pan in the 400°F oven.
Mix the seasoned flour and dip the chicken in it.
Lay the chicken in the pan in one layer, skin side down.
Bake 30 minutes, then turn it.
Bake until tender, about 30 minutes more.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.serve_with: Mashed potatoes and green beans

rows.title: Chicken and Rice: Easy!
rows.dek: A family favorite dump-and-bake dinner in the American casserole tradition, built on canned condensed soup and a packet of onion soup mix. Everything goes in one dish and the oven does the rest.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Mix the soup, water and onion soup mix.
Stir in the rice with a fork.
Put the chicken in the bottom of a 9×13 pan.
Pour the rice mixture over the chicken.
Cover with foil and bake 1 hour at 350°F.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.serve_with: Steamed green beans and a green salad

rows.title: Chicken & Broccoli
rows.dek: A family favorite, a home version of chicken divan, the old New York hotel dish. Home cooks swapped its rich sauce for canned soup and mayonnaise, and it became a weeknight classic.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 packages (10 oz) frozen broccoli, or fresh
steps: Simmer the chicken 20 minutes, then bone and skin it and cut it into bite-size pieces.
Cook the broccoli 4 minutes; it must stay crisp.
Lay the broccoli end to end in a shallow baking dish and spread the chicken over it.
Mix the soup, mayonnaise, lemon juice and curry powder and pour it over the chicken.
Sprinkle the cheese on top, then the bread crumbs.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°F.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.serve_with: Baked Rice and a green salad

rows.title: Baked Rice
rows.dek: A family favorite: rice that cooks gently in a covered dish in the oven, with no pot to watch. Fluffy, savory and easy to feed a crowd.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Use an ungreased 1½-quart casserole dish with a tight lid (or foil).
Put everything in and cover it.
Bake 45 minutes at 375°F. Don't peek and don't stir.
Fluff with a fork when serving.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.serve_with: Chicken Delight or Pollo Guisado

rows.title: Taco Pie
rows.dek: A family favorite Tex-Mex casserole built on refrigerated crescent dough. Taco filling, Fritos and cheese bake into a pie that cuts into neat wedges.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Fresh avocados and salsa, to serve
steps: Brown the beef and drain it.
Add the seasoning and water and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the corn and olives.
Press the crescent dough into an ungreased pie pan for the crust.
Sprinkle half the Fritos on the crust.
Layer the meat, sour cream, cheese, then the rest of the Fritos.
Bake 25 minutes at 375°F.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.serve_with: Guacamole, Mexican rice and refried beans
rows.pairs_with: Mexican Coke or agua de jamaica

rows.title: Garbanzo Spread for Sandwiches
rows.dek: A family recipe card favorite, this sandwich spread is built on chickpeas, one of the oldest crops on earth, first domesticated thousands of years ago in what is now southeastern Turkey. Fun fact: the name garbanzo comes from Spanish, from the Old Spanish word arvanço.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can (15½ oz) garbanzo beans, drained and chopped
steps: Mix everything except the sprouts.
Serve with the sprouts on rye, pita or toasted sourdough.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.serve_with: Fresh fruit and a green salad

rows.title: Mulled Citrus Punch
rows.dek: A warm, spiced citrus punch for the holidays. It simmers on the stove, fills the house with a good smell and keeps warm for the whole party.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Boil the 2 cups water and the sugar together 5 minutes.
Add the rest of the ingredients and bring it to a boil.
Turn the burner down and simmer 30 minutes.
Take out the cinnamon sticks and cloves before serving.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Peachie Cinnamon Whirligigs
rows.dek: Cinnamon-roll slices baked on hot peach sauce, so the bottoms soak it up and the tops turn golden. A splendid finale for a chicken dinner.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can (29 oz) sliced peaches, with syrup
¼ cup sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Cook the peaches, syrup and cornstarch over medium heat, stirring, until thick; boil 1 minute and keep hot.
Stir the baking mix, 2 tbsp sugar, melted butter and milk to a soft dough; knead 8 to 10 times.
Roll to a 9-inch square, spread with the softened butter and sprinkle with the cinnamon sugar.
Roll up, seal, cut 1-inch slices and set them cut side up on the hot peaches in an 8x8 pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes. Serve warm, with cream if you like.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Mile High Strawberry Pie
rows.dek: One box of frozen strawberries becomes a towering pink pie. A long beating whips so much air into the filling that it climbs far above the crust. The secret: don't stop the beaters.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1½ cups flour, 1½ tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt (crust)
steps: Stir the flour, sugar and salt in the pie tin with the milk and oil, and press up the edges.
Bake the crust at 425°F for 10 to 15 minutes and let it cool.
Beat the whites, sugar, berries and lemon juice on high for 10 minutes without stopping.
Whip the cream and fold it in.
Pile it into the crust, freeze, and serve frozen.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: For a 9x13 pan, make 1½ times the crust.
rows.serve_with: Any summer barbecue or holiday dinner

rows.title: Cherry Bars
rows.dek: A big-pan bar for a crowd: buttery almond and vanilla dough, cherry pie filling in the middle, more dough dropped on top and a thin glaze. The secret is room-temperature eggs and butter.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1½ tsp each vanilla and almond extract
Glaze, 1 cup confectioner's sugar and 3 tbsp milk
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line a 12x17 jelly roll pan with foil and spray it.
Cream the butter and sugar 1 to 2 minutes, then mix in the salt, eggs, vanilla and almond.
Mix in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Set aside 1¾ cups of dough and press the rest into the pan.
Spread the cherry pie filling over it and drop the reserved dough on top in small pieces.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes, until golden, and cool completely on a rack.
Whisk the glaze, drizzle it over and cut into 35 squares.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Buddha Bowl
rows.dek: A recipe from avocado growers that uses avocado two ways: blended into a creamy tahini dressing and grilled until charred. Roasted spiced vegetables and quinoa make it a full meal in one bowl.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 tsp each chili powder and cumin
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Toss ¼ cup oil with the sweet potato, carrot, zucchini, spices, salt and pepper; roast until golden, about 40 minutes.
Blend the rest of the oil, the tahini, 1 avocado and lemon juice, adding water to thin.
Heat a grill to medium-high, oil the other avocado, grill it cut side down to char, then peel and slice it.
Divide the quinoa, vegetables and avocado into 2 bowls and drizzle with the dressing.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: No grill? Char the avocado halves cut side down in a hot cast iron pan.

rows.title: Lemonade
rows.dek: Real lemonade the long way: strips of lemon peel steeped in hot sugar syrup give it a deep lemon flavor before the fresh juice goes in. Chill it very cold and pour it over ice with a lemon slice.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ⅔ cup lemon peel in 2" x ¼" strips (about 4 lemons)
Ice and lemon slices, to serve
steps: In a large pitcher, combine the sugar, lemon peel and hot water.
Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Refrigerate until very cold.
Stir in the cold water and lemon juice.
Pour over ice and add a lemon slice.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.serve_with: Any summer dinner

rows.title: Watermelon Lemonade
rows.dek: Tart lemonade with fresh watermelon puree in sugar-rimmed glasses. Pour it layered, with the pink on top.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 3 cups fresh lemon juice (12 to 15 lemons)
2 cups watermelon puree (seedless watermelon, blended smooth)
Lemon half and superfine sugar, for the glasses
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the lemon juice, then add the water and stir.
Blend seedless watermelon chunks until smooth for the puree.
Stir in the puree, or keep it separate to pour layered.
Rub the glass rims with half a lemon and dip them in superfine sugar.
Fill with ice and lemonade, spoon the puree on top if layering, and garnish with lemon slices.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Mango Tango Smoothie
rows.dek: A bright tropical smoothie: pineapple and orange juice blended with frozen mango, banana and pineapple sherbet. Serve it right away while it's thick and frosty.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Pour the pineapple and orange juice into the blender.
Add the frozen banana, sherbet and mango.
Blend on a low setting for 30 seconds, then on high until smooth.
Serve immediately.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Frosty Orange Cooler
rows.dek: A sparkling party punch from an old lemon-juice ad: orange juice, lemon and ginger ale poured over scoops of orange sherbet, so it foams up like a float. Add the ginger ale at the last minute to keep the fizz.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can (6 oz) frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
steps: In a pitcher, combine the water, juice concentrate, lemon juice and sugar, and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Chill.
Just before serving, add the ginger ale.
Scoop sherbet into glasses and pour the juice mixture over it.
Garnish as you like.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Frosty Strawberry Pops
rows.dek: A light summer freezer treat from a newspaper clipping: fresh strawberries blended with evaporated milk and a little juice concentrate, frozen in paper cups on craft sticks.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 3 tbsp frozen orange, cranberry or pineapple juice concentrate
steps: Blend everything about 1 minute, until smooth.
Pour into eight 3-ounce paper cups set in a shallow pan.
Put a wooden craft stick or plastic spoon in the center of each.
Freeze until firm, about 4 hours, then store in a freezer bag.
To release, dip each cup briefly in water up to the rim.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Lemonade or Limeade Base
rows.dek: A make-ahead lemonade base from an old newspaper clipping: a quick sugar syrup, fresh lemon juice with its pulp, and twisted strips of peel for the oils. Keep it in the fridge or freeze it as cubes.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Peel from 2 lemons, cut in strips (colored part only)
1 cup lemon juice (about 4 to 5 big lemons), with pulp, no seeds
For limeade: 8 to 9 fresh limes, peel from 1 to 2 of them
To serve: ice, and club soda or water
steps: In a small saucepan, boil the sugar and water for 3 to 4 minutes, then cool.
Twist each strip of peel over a pitcher or jar to release the oils, then drop the strips in.
Stir in the lemon juice and the cooled syrup.
Refrigerate; the base keeps for days, or strain and freeze it in an ice-cube tray and bag the cubes.
For each glass, use 1/4 to 1/3 cup of base or the same in frozen cubes, add ice, and fill with club soda or water.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: The syrup keeps indefinitely in the fridge, so make a double or triple batch for sweetening fruit too.

rows.title: Almost Homemade Lemonade
rows.dek: A shortcut from an old newspaper clipping: a whole lemon, rind and all, pulsed and steeped in thawed frozen concentrate, then strained. The rind's oils make store-bought lemonade taste fresh-squeezed, and the empty can measures the water and ice.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can (12 oz) frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed
1 fresh lemon, washed and patted dry
3 cans water (use the empty concentrate can)
steps: Cut the lemon into chunks, rind and all.
Pulse it to bits in a food processor.
Stir the chopped lemon into the thawed concentrate.
Let it sit at room temperature for an hour or two.
Strain into a pitcher, pressing on the lemon bits.
Add 3 cans of water and 1½ cans of ice, and stir.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start it a couple of hours before guests arrive; the lemon needs time to steep.

rows.title: Blueberry Bombe
rows.dek: A light, mousse-like dessert from an old gelatine ad: blueberries blended with milk and gelatine, whisked into whipped topping and chilled in little cups. Top with whipped topping and grated lemon peel, or freeze it for a cool summer treat.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 package (12 oz) frozen unsweetened blueberries or strawberries, rinsed
2 cups frozen whipped topping, thawed, plus more to garnish
steps: Sprinkle the gelatine over the cold milk in a blender and let it stand 2 minutes.
Add the hot milk and blend on low until the gelatine is completely dissolved, about 2 minutes.
Add the blueberries and sugar and blend until smooth.
Pour into a large bowl and whisk in the whipped topping.
Pour into 8 dessert cups and chill until firm, about 3 hours.
Garnish with whipped topping and grated lemon peel.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: For a frozen bombe, freeze the cups 3 hours or until firm, then let them stand at room temperature 15 minutes before serving.

rows.title: Brazilian Lemonade
rows.dek: Not lemonade at all: whole limes, rind and all, pulsed with sugar, water, ice and a spoonful of sweetened condensed milk, then strained. It comes out pale, creamy and tart. Pulse just five times so the rinds don't turn bitter.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Wash the limes well, cut off the ends and slice each into eight wedges.
Put the limes, sugar, sweetened condensed milk, water and ice in a blender.
Pulse 5 times, no more.
Strain through a fine mesh strainer to remove the rinds.
Serve right away over ice.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Blending longer makes it bitter, so stop at five pulses.

rows.title: Hawaiian Meatballs
rows.dek: A sweet-and-sour skillet supper: ginger beef meatballs browned in one pan, then simmered in a glossy pineapple, cider-vinegar and soy sauce with green pepper. Serve with toothpicks as a party bite or over rice.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ⅔ cup panko breadcrumbs and ½ cup minced onion
1 egg and ¾ tsp ground ginger
2 Tbsp cornstarch and ½ cup brown sugar
1 (13½-oz) can pineapple tidbits, juice drained and reserved
steps: Mix the beef, panko, onion, egg and ginger, and shape into 1- to 2-inch balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil over medium heat, about 10 minutes.
Remove the meatballs from the pan and set them aside.
In the same pan, mix the cornstarch, brown sugar, pineapple juice, vinegar and soy sauce.
Simmer over medium-low heat, stirring until the sauce thickens.
Add the pineapple, green pepper and meatballs and heat 5 to 7 minutes, until the meat reaches 160°F.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Serve with toothpicks as an appetizer, or spoon over rice for dinner.

rows.title: The Whole Bowl
rows.dek: A copycat of a favorite bowl-shop dish: brown rice and beans layered with pico, sharp cheddar, olives, sour cream and avocado, all under a golden, garlicky Tali sauce blended from chickpeas, lemon and nutritional yeast.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can black beans, drained (or a mix of red and black)
½ cup salsa or pico de gallo; ¼ cup black olives, roughly chopped
½ to 1 cup sharp cheddar, grated
¼ cup sour cream; 1 avocado, sliced; ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped
Tali sauce: ¼ cup each virgin olive oil, water and nutritional yeast
Tali sauce: juice of 1 lemon, 3 garlic cloves, ⅓ cup drained chickpeas
Tali sauce: ¼ tsp each cumin, curry powder, turmeric, garlic salt, onion salt and salt
Tali sauce: ½ tsp mustard powder, ⅛ tsp cayenne pepper
steps: Blend all the Tali sauce ingredients in a food processor until silky smooth, adding water 1 tablespoon at a time to thin it.
In each bowl, layer 1 cup brown rice and a quarter of the beans.
Add 2 tablespoons pico, half of that bowl's Tali sauce, 2 tablespoons cheddar and 1 tablespoon olives.
Top with 1 tablespoon sour cream and the rest of the Tali sauce (about ¼ cup sauce per bowl in all).
Finish with a quarter of the avocado, sliced, and a generous pinch of cilantro.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Make the sauce first; it keeps in the fridge.

rows.title: Ham and Potato Casserole
rows.dek: A set-and-forget slow-cooker supper: red potatoes, thin-sliced ham, poblano strips, olive oil and oregano cook low all day, then go into a dish under melted Monterey Jack and fresh cilantro. Use as much or as little poblano as you like.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1½ lb red potatoes, peeled and sliced
2 poblano chili peppers, cut into thin strips (optional, to taste)
1 tbsp dried oregano leaves and ¼ tsp salt
1 cup (4 oz) shredded Monterey Jack cheese, with or without hot peppers
steps: Put everything except the cheese and cilantro in the slow cooker and mix well.
Cover and cook on LOW 7 hours or on HIGH 4 hours.
Move the potato mixture to a serving dish.
Sprinkle with the cheese and cilantro and let stand 3 minutes, until the cheese melts.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Use one poblano, or none, for a milder dish.

rows.title: Hot Buttered Rum Mix
rows.dek: A winter mug-warmer: butter, brown sugar and warm spices mixed into a batter you keep in a jar. Stir a spoonful into hot water for a sweet, spiced, butterscotch-like drink.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ⅛ tsp ground cardamom and a pinch of ground cloves
steps: Mix the butter, brown sugar and spices together well.
Put the mix in an airtight container; it keeps for 2 weeks.
For each mug, stir 1½ to 2 tablespoons of the mix into ½ cup hot water.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Fill a small jar with the mix for a Christmas gift.

rows.title: Linguine Carbonara
rows.dek: An American weeknight carbonara with no eggs: crisp bacon, onion and garlic, a quick milk sauce with sour cream and Parmesan, spooned over hot linguine.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ½ cup chopped red onion and 3 cloves garlic, minced
2 Tbsp dried parsley, salt and pepper to taste
steps: Cook the linguine according to the package, drain and keep warm.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium-high heat, stirring, until golden brown.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until translucent and soft, then stir in the oregano and basil.
Add the flour and stir to coat.
Turn the heat to medium, stir in the milk and simmer gently until the sauce thickens.
Off the heat, whisk in the sour cream, Parmesan, parsley, salt and pepper, and serve over the hot linguine.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Add 1 cup cooked peas for something green.

rows.title: Citrus Couscous
rows.dek: A bright, chilled couscous salad: couscous soaked in hot citrus juices, tossed with onion, parsley and mint, a lemon-paprika dressing, raisins and toasted almonds.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ¾ cup water and ¼ cup orange juice
½ cup lemon juice from concentrate, divided
2 tbsp each chopped fresh parsley and mint
¼ cup olive oil, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp paprika
steps: Put the water, lime juice, orange juice and ¼ cup lemon juice in a large microwave-safe bowl.
Microwave on high 3 minutes, until boiling.
Stir in the couscous, onion, parsley and mint until the liquid is absorbed.
Let it cool, fluffing now and then with a fork.
Whisk the remaining ¼ cup lemon juice with the oil, salt and paprika.
Toss the dressing, raisins and almonds gently into the couscous and chill.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Make it a few hours ahead.

rows.title: Ham and Egg Pie
rows.dek: A contest-winning egg pie: a quick oil-and-milk crust that needs no chilling, filled with eggs, cottage cheese, two cheeses, ham, salami and green onion. It bakes up like a hearty quiche for a holiday brunch.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Crust, 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 Tbsp baking powder and ½ tsp salt
½ cup milk and ⅓ cup cooking oil
½ cup each shredded sharp cheddar and mozzarella (2 oz each)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Stir the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl and make a well.
Pour in the milk and oil all at once and stir until moistened.
Knead gently 10 to 12 strokes, roll to a 12-inch circle and line a 9-inch pie plate, crimping the edge.
Stir together the eggs, cottage cheese, cheeses, ham, salami, green onion and parsley and pour into the crust.
Bake 50 to 55 minutes, until a knife near the center comes out clean, covering the edge with foil if it browns too fast.
Let stand 10 minutes before cutting.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: The oil crust needs no chilling.

rows.title: Cheesy Brunch Squares
rows.dek: A make-ahead breakfast bake: eggs and half-and-half over hash browns, broccoli, cheddar, ham and onion, topped with bread crumbs. Mix it the night before.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 tsp Italian seasoning, 1 clove garlic (minced), ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper
4 cups frozen hash brown potatoes, thawed
1 package (16 oz) frozen chopped broccoli, thawed and drained
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 13x9x2-inch baking pan well.
In a large bowl, mix the eggs, half-and-half, Italian seasoning, garlic, salt and pepper.
Stir in the potatoes, broccoli, cheese, ham and onion.
Pour into the pan and sprinkle with the bread crumbs.
Bake 45 minutes, until bubbly, then cut into 12 squares.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: For make-ahead, add the crumbs just before baking.

rows.title: Sunrise Breakfast Casserole
rows.dek: A make-ahead breakfast bake from an old newspaper clipping: sausage, hash browns and cheese in a mustard egg custard, baked golden in the morning.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 packages (12 oz each) breakfast sausage links
1½ tsp ground mustard, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper
1 package (30 oz) frozen shredded hash browns, thawed
2 cups (8 oz) shredded 4-cheese Mexican blend cheese
½ cup diced red bell pepper
⅓ cup thinly sliced green onions
steps: Bake the sausage links on an ungreased 15x10x1-inch pan at 375°F for 15 to 20 minutes, turning once, until browned; drain.
Cool the sausage slightly and slice it into ¼-inch coins.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard, salt and pepper in a large bowl, then stir in the sausage, hash browns, cheese, bell pepper and onions.
Pour into a greased 13x9x2-inch baking dish, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Take it out 30 minutes before baking, then bake uncovered at 350°F for 65 to 70 minutes, until a knife in the center comes out clean.
Let it stand 10 minutes and serve with salsa or picante sauce.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Assemble it the night before.

rows.title: Fab Rice Pilaf
rows.dek: A one-pot side: rice toasted golden in olive oil, then simmered in chicken broth with garlic, onion, green pepper, basil and chunks of small zucchini. Finish with fresh tomatoes and Parmesan on top.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ½ cup each chopped onion and chopped green pepper
Chopped fresh tomatoes and grated Parmesan cheese, for the top
steps: Warm the olive oil in a 2-quart pot and brown the rice.
Add the garlic, onion and green pepper and let them soften.
Add the broth, basil and zucchini and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat down, put the lid on and simmer 20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Top with chopped fresh tomatoes and Parmesan cheese and serve.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: For brown rice, simmer 30 minutes.

rows.title: Cheesy Hash Brown Skillet Dinner
rows.dek: A one-skillet supper: ground beef, onion and mushrooms crisped with hash browns, then Italian tomatoes and melted cheddar. Press the potatoes down and leave them alone.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 package (20 oz) refrigerated shredded hash browns
2 cans (14.5 oz each) Italian seasoned diced tomatoes, undrained
steps: In a 12-inch nonstick skillet, cook the beef and onion until browned (160°F).
Stir in the hash browns and mushrooms, spread them flat and press down lightly.
Cook 6 to 7 minutes, until golden brown on the bottom.
Drizzle with the oil and turn the potatoes over in sections with a spatula.
Cook 6 to 8 minutes more, until golden and tender, turning again if needed.
Stir in the tomatoes and salt until hot, then top with cheese and cook until melted.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Refrigerate any leftovers.

rows.title: Lasagna
rows.dek: An old-fashioned family lasagna: a beef and tomato sauce simmered low for two hours, layered with noodles and sliced mozzarella, then finished with Parmesan or cheddar. A Sunday pan that feeds a crowd.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1½ medium onions, chopped, and 2 tbsp butter
2 tbsp parsley, 1 tsp basil, 2 tsp Italian seasonings, ¼ tsp pepper
steps: Brown the hamburger and onions in the butter.
Add the herbs, seasonings, pepper, tomato sauce, tomato paste and water.
Cover and cook 2 hours over low heat, stirring now and then.
In a buttered 9x13 dish, layer noodles, sauce and sliced mozzarella, and repeat.
End with noodles and sauce, sprinkle with Parmesan or cheddar, and bake at 350°F for 30 minutes.
Let it cool about 30 minutes before serving.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: No cottage cheese, and use sliced mozzarella only, never shredded.

rows.title: Taco Casserole
rows.dek: A family weeknight favorite: chili-bean beef layered over broken tortilla chips, spread with sour cream, then topped with green onions, tomato and cheese and baked just until melted. Serve with more chips and shredded lettuce.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 to 4 tsp chili powder and 1 tsp garlic powder
2 cups coarsely broken tortilla chips, plus more to serve
1 cup sour cream or plain yogurt
½ cup sliced green onions and 1 tomato, chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Brown the ground beef and drain it.
Stir in the beans, tomato sauce, chili powder and garlic powder, and bring to a boil.
Spread the chips in an ungreased 2-quart casserole dish and top with the beef mixture.
Spread the sour cream over the beef, then sprinkle with green onions, tomato and cheese.
Bake uncovered 23 minutes, until the cheese melts.
Serve with more chips and shredded lettuce.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Use garlic powder, not garlic salt, so the casserole isn't too salty.

rows.title: Saucy Meatballs
rows.dek: Beef and Parmesan meatballs browned in a skillet, then simmered in chunky tomatoes sharpened with steak sauce until the sauce thickens. Spooned over hot buttered noodles, one pound of beef feeds five on a weeknight.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ½ cup seasoned dry bread crumbs
½ cup milk and 1 egg, slightly beaten
⅓ to ½ cup steak sauce and ½ tsp salt
steps: Mix the beef, Parmesan, bread crumbs, milk and egg.
Shape into 20 meatballs, a rounded tablespoon each.
Brown them well in the shortening and drain off the fat.
Sprinkle the flour over the meatballs and stir gently to coat.
Mix the tomatoes, steak sauce and salt, pour over and simmer uncovered about 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over hot buttered noodles.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Simmer longer for a thicker sauce.

rows.title: Tuna Cheese Biscuit Casserole
rows.dek: A one-dish supper: tuna and peas in a creamy soup sauce with green pepper, onion and a little lemon, topped with cheddar pinwheel biscuits rolled up like cinnamon rolls and baked golden.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ⅓ cup each chopped green pepper and chopped onion
2¼ cups biscuit baking mix (¼ cup for the sauce, 2 cups for the biscuits)
1 can cream of mushroom or celery soup
1 can (8½ oz) peas and 1 can (6½ oz) tuna, both drained
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Sauté the pepper and onion in the shortening until tender, then stir in ¼ cup baking mix and the soup.
Gradually stir in the milk, bring to a boil over medium heat while stirring, and boil 1 minute.
Stir in the peas, tuna and lemon juice, pour into a 9x9 baking dish and keep it hot.
Stir 2 cups baking mix with the water to a soft dough, beat 20 strokes, and knead 5 times on a floured board.
Roll into a 9x15 rectangle, sprinkle with the cheese, roll up tightly from the wide side, seal, and cut 12 slices.
Set the slices seam side down on the hot tuna mixture and bake 20 to 25 minutes, until golden.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Keep the filling hot while you make the biscuits.

rows.title: Feijoada (Tangy Black Beans)
rows.dek: A simple Brazilian-style black bean pot from two old newspaper clippings: beans simmered slow with onion, garlic, celery, tomato and a whole orange for the tang. A ladle of mashed beans stirred back in makes it thick and glossy.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 large onion, chopped, and 2 cloves garlic, minced
3 cups stock or water (water keeps it vegetarian)
1 bay leaf and ¼ tsp pepper
steps: Sauté the onion and garlic in oil in a heavy, large pot.
Add the beans, stock or water, bay leaf and pepper, bring to a boil and simmer 2 minutes.
Cover, take off the heat and let sit 1 hour.
Add the orange, salt, celery and tomato and simmer with the lid ajar 2 to 3 hours, until the beans are tender.
Mash a ladleful of beans, stir them back in and cook until the pot thickens.
Take out the orange and bay leaf and serve over white rice.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: It can all be done in a pressure cooker after sautéing the onion and garlic; much quicker and still very good.

rows.title: Corn Casserole
rows.dek: A five-ingredient holiday side from a magazine clipping: two kinds of canned corn, corn muffin mix, sour cream and an egg stirred in one bowl and baked into a soft, spoonable corn pudding with golden edges.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 13x9 baking dish with cooking spray.
In a large bowl, mix both corns, the muffin mix, sour cream and egg until well blended.
Spoon the mixture into the prepared dish.
Bake 30 minutes, until golden and set.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Drain the canned kernels well so the center sets soft, not soggy.

rows.title: Summer Pasta with Grilled Shrimp
rows.dek: A summer pasta: diced tomatoes, basil, garlic and olive oil stirred raw into a bright sauce, tossed with hot linguine and garlicky grilled shrimp.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1½ lb tomatoes (about 5 medium), cut into ½-inch dice
¾ lb linguine or other pasta
steps: Toss the shrimp with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the garlic, salt and pepper, and heat the grill.
Thread the shrimp on skewers.
In a large bowl, combine the tomatoes, the remaining 6 tbsp oil and garlic, the basil, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water until just done, about 12 minutes, and drain.
Grill the shrimp, turning once, until just done, about 3 minutes in all.
Toss the pasta with the shrimp and tomato mixture and serve.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: No grill? Sauté the shrimp over high heat after the pasta is cooked.
rows.pairs_with: Lightly dressed green salad, French bread, and sorbet with shortbread cookies

rows.title: Bar-B-Que Beans
rows.dek: A slow-cooker bean medley for a crowd: kidney, pinto, pork and beans and green beans with sautéed green pepper and green onion in a sweet brown sugar and chili sauce, crumbled bacon on top. It keeps warm on low as long as the party lasts.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 cans kidney beans and 2 cans pinto beans
steps: Drain the beans and put them in the slow cooker.
Cook the bacon and set it aside.
Sauté the green pepper and green onions and add them to the beans.
Mix the brown sugar and chili sauce and stir it into the beans.
Cover and cook on high for 2 to 3 hours.
Turn to low, add the crumbled bacon and serve any time.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: It holds on low for hours, so it is made for potlucks.

rows.title: Ham and Cheese Mashed Potatoes
rows.dek: Leftover mashed potatoes turned into a casserole: garlic-salted potatoes, a layer of diced ham, and whipped cream folded with cheddar that puffs up golden in a hot oven. Food-storage potato pearls and canned ham work too.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and grease a 1½-quart baking dish.
In a bowl, combine the potatoes and garlic salt.
Spread the potatoes into the dish and sprinkle the ham over them.
Fold the cheese into the whipped cream and spoon it over the ham.
Bake uncovered 15 minutes, or until golden brown.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Instant potato pearls and canned ham from food storage work just as well.

rows.title: Taco Soup
rows.dek: A thirty-minute pot of beef, beans, corn and tomatoes simmered with taco seasoning, straight from the pantry shelf. Top each bowl with avocado, cheese, sour cream or corn chips. It tastes even better the next day.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can (16 oz) kidney beans, with liquid
To garnish, avocado, cheese, sour cream or corn chips
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large stock pot.
Add the onion and mix it in.
Add the tomatoes, corn, beans, tomato sauce and taco seasoning.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Serve with avocado, cheese, sour cream or corn chips if you like.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Make it ahead; it reheats well.

rows.title: Boston Baked Beans
rows.dek: Old New England baked beans the slow way: dry navy beans, molasses, brown sugar, dry mustard, salt pork and onion, left in the slow cooker on low for two or three days until tender, dark and glossy.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 cups dry navy or small white beans
1 tsp salt and 1 tsp dry mustard
steps: Put everything into the slow cooker.
Cook on low for two to three days.
Check and stir now and then until the beans are tender.
If they look dry, add more water a little at a time.
With no slow cooker, bake in a heavy crock at 200°F for two to three days, stirring and watching the water.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start it two or three days before you need it; it holds well on low.

rows.title: Original Lentil Soup
rows.dek: A restaurant-style lentil soup: bacon and vegetables softened in oil, thickened with flour, then simmered low for three hours with lentils, potatoes and beef base until thick and hearty.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 3 oz salad oil and 3 oz bacon, diced
¾ cup each carrots, onion and celery, diced
2 tsp all-in-one seasoning (or 2 tsp celery seed)
2 tsp MSG and 4 Tbsp beef base
Pinch each nutmeg and white pepper; salt to taste
steps: Heat the oil in a large double boiler or large pot.
Add the bacon, carrots, onion and celery and sauté until the onion and celery are transparent.
Stirring constantly, add the flour.
When the flour is blended in, slowly add the water, stirring constantly.
Add the lentils, salt, seasoning, MSG, beef base, nutmeg, white pepper and potatoes.
Simmer about 3 hours.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: 2 tsp celery seed can replace the all-in-one seasoning. Taste before salting; the beef base is salty.

rows.title: Cheeseburger Skillet Dinner
rows.dek: A weeknight skillet that tastes like a cheeseburger: browned beef and onion with ketchup and mustard, a bag of frozen mixed vegetables, melted cheddar, and a box of mac and cheese stirred in at the end. One pan, about half an hour.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ⅓ cup ketchup and ¼ cup water
½ tsp prepared mustard and ¼ tsp garlic powder
steps: Make the macaroni and cheese as directed on the package.
Brown the meat and onion in a large skillet, then drain.
Stir in the vegetables, ketchup, water, mustard and garlic powder.
Cook until the vegetables are crisp-tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the cheese and stir until melted.
Mix in the macaroni and cheese and season with salt and pepper.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Ground turkey works just as well as beef.

rows.title: Shepherd's Pie
rows.dek: A weeknight shepherd's pie with a twist: browned beef, onion and green pepper go into BBQ sauce, then corn or green beans and quick mashed potatoes on top, with cheddar over the top before it bakes.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 cups cooked corn or green beans
Pepper, garlic powder and chili powder
Shredded cheddar cheese, for the top
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Brown the beef with the onion and green pepper, drain, and stir in the BBQ sauce.
Boil the water, add the potato pearls and spices, cover for 5 minutes, then stir.
In a pie plate or medium casserole, layer the meat, then the corn or beans, then the potatoes.
Cover the top with cheddar cheese.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until bubbly.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start with ½ cup BBQ sauce and add more to taste; a smoky sauce works best.

rows.title: Buckaroo Short Ribs and Noodles
rows.dek: A cowboy-style one-pot braise: boneless short ribs simmered tender in a sweet-tangy ketchup, soy and Worcestershire gravy, tossed with wide noodles and stewed tomatoes.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 lb boneless beef short ribs, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 cup chopped onion and 2 cloves garlic, mashed
½ cup beef broth plus 1 Tbsp vinegar
2 Tbsp soy sauce and 1 Tbsp Worcestershire sauce
2 cups cold water mixed with ¼ cup cornstarch
steps: Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and stir-fry the ribs until browned on all sides.
Add the onion, garlic, ketchup, broth and vinegar, soy sauce and Worcestershire.
Mix the water with the cornstarch and stir it into the pot.
Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover with the lid slightly ajar and simmer 1½ hours, until the meat is tender.
Cook the noodles per the package, drain well, and add the drained tomatoes.
Spoon off excess fat from the meat and stir in the noodles.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Pasta with Scallops and Lemon Garlic Butter
rows.dek: A quick dinner that feels like a restaurant: big sea scallops seared in butter, olive oil, garlic and lemon zest, then spooned over fettuccine tossed with fresh chervil. It all comes together while the pasta cooks.
rows.image_alt: Pasta with Scallops and Lemon Garlic Butter
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Cook the pasta according to the package directions.
Meanwhile, melt the butter and oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the garlic and cook until translucent.
Add the lemon zest and cook 1 minute.
Add the scallops and cook 20 to 30 seconds on each side, until just opaque.
Drain the pasta, toss with the chervil, and top with the scallops and lemon garlic butter sauce.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Pat the scallops dry first; large ones may need a bit longer to turn opaque in the middle.

rows.title: Meat Kebabs (Morocco)
rows.dek: Moroccan-style kofta: ground beef or lamb with grated onion, parsley, cilantro, cumin, paprika and pepper, rested an hour, then shaped on skewers and grilled. Great with herb rice.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Combine the meat, herbs, onion and spices and let stand one hour.
Shape the mixture into long sausage shapes around the skewers.
Broil or barbecue, turning frequently, for 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve hot with herb rice.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Squeeze the grated onion dry so the meat holds on the skewers.

rows.title: Escabeche
rows.dek: White fish dredged in flour and fried golden, then folded gently into a quick sweet-and-sour sauce of lemon, brown sugar and soy with mushrooms, green pepper, ginger and green onion. A fast one-pan dinner served hot.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 to 3 lb red snapper, bass, tuna or any white fish, filleted and cut in serving pieces
Salt to taste and flour to coat
1 cup sliced mushrooms and 2 cloves garlic, minced
1 large green pepper, cut in strips
1 tsp fresh ginger, cut in fine strips
2 Tbsp lemon juice, 1 cup water, 1½ Tbsp brown sugar, 1 Tbsp soy sauce
steps: Heat 2 Tbsp oil in a fry pan.
Salt the fish, coat it with flour and fry until brown, then remove it and set aside.
Add 1 Tbsp oil with the mushrooms, green pepper, ginger and garlic and fry 1 minute.
Add the green onion and stir-fry a few seconds.
Add the lemon juice, water, sugar and soy sauce, then thicken with the cornstarch.
Gently add the fish and stir without breaking it, and serve hot.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Stir the cornstarch into a few spoons of the water first so it doesn't lump.

rows.title: Bombones de Arroz
rows.dek: Little rice fritters: cooked rice, egg, vanilla and coconut, dropped by the spoonful into hot oil until golden, then buried in powdered sugar. Crisp outside, soft inside, and best eaten hot.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 3 Tbsp sugar and ½ tsp vanilla
1 Tbsp baking powder and a pinch of salt
steps: Mix the rice, eggs, sugar and vanilla well in a bowl.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together and stir them into the rice mixture.
Stir in the coconut.
Heat the oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 350°F.
Drop tablespoonfuls into the hot oil one at a time and fry until golden brown on all sides.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve hot.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Day-old leftover rice works fine; a heavy pot with 2 to 3 inches of oil and a thermometer stands in for a deep fryer.

rows.title: Scandinavian Meatballs with Dill Sauce
rows.dek: A beef cook-off recipe from an old newspaper: tender meatballs with rye bread, grated apple, raisins and almonds, browned in a hot oven and covered in a creamy dill sauce with crunchy water chestnuts. Stir the yogurt in off the heat.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 eggs, beaten, and 1 cup heavy cream
½ cup each grated apple and chopped raisins
¼ cup chopped almonds and 4 tsp chopped green onion
1 tsp each salt and white pepper
Sauce, ¼ cup butter, ¼ cup flour and 2 cups beef bouillon
1½ tsp dried dill weed and 1 cup sliced water chestnuts
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and set a rack in a roasting pan.
Gently but thoroughly mix the beef, eggs, cream, bread cubes, apple, raisins, almonds, green onion, salt and pepper.
Shape into 2-inch meatballs, set them on the rack and bake 10 to 15 minutes, until brown.
For the sauce, melt the butter, stir in the flour, then add the bouillon, a pinch of salt and the dill and cook over medium heat until thick.
Stir in the water chestnuts, take the pan off the heat and stir in the yogurt.
Put the meatballs in a chafing or serving dish and pour the sauce over.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Adding the yogurt off the heat keeps the sauce from curdling.

rows.title: El Dorado Beef Casserole
rows.dek: A layered Mexican-style casserole: crushed tortilla chips, seasoned beef with tomato sauce and olives, a sour cream and cottage cheese layer with green chiles, and Monterey Jack, twice over, with broken chips on top.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 Tbsp dried diced onions and ½ tsp garlic powder
1 cup sour cream and 1 cup cottage cheese
steps: Fry the ground beef and drain off the fat.
Stir in the onion, garlic powder, tomato sauce and olives.
In a separate bowl, combine the sour cream, cottage cheese and green chiles.
In the buttered dish, layer half the chips (crushed), half the meat, half the sour cream mixture and half the cheese.
Repeat the layers and end with several broken chips on top.
Bake covered at 350°F for 30 to 35 minutes.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Layer it ahead and bake when people arrive.

rows.title: White Chicken Enchiladas
rows.dek: A creamy, mild enchilada: chicken and Monterey Jack rolled in flour tortillas, covered in a quick sour-cream sauce with green chiles, then baked until the cheese bubbles.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix the chicken with 1 cup of the cheese.
Roll the filling up in the tortillas and set them seam down in a 9x13 pan.
Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute, stirring.
Whisk in the broth until smooth, and when it thickens, turn off the heat.
Stir in the sour cream and chiles until smooth, pour the sauce over the enchiladas and top with the rest of the cheese.
Bake 25 minutes, until bubbly.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: A rotisserie chicken gives you the 2 cups of shredded chicken.

rows.title: Rustler's Pie
rows.dek: A shortcut cottage pie from a three-ingredient magazine clipping: beef tips in gravy baked with broccoli, corn and red peppers, then topped with four mounds of jalapeño-Cheddar mashed potatoes and baked until bubbly. Eight minutes of work.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 package (17 oz) refrigerated beef tips with gravy
1 bag (1 lb) frozen broccoli, corn and red peppers, thawed
1 package (1 lb) refrigerated russet jalapeño mashed potatoes with Cheddar
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Have a 1½-quart shallow baking dish ready.
Heat the beef tips in the microwave as the package directs, then mix them with the vegetables in the baking dish.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 15 minutes, until steaming hot, then stir.
Meanwhile, heat the potatoes in the microwave as the package directs.
Spoon the potatoes in 4 mounds over the meat and vegetables.
Bake uncovered 15 minutes, until bubbly. Garnish with chopped parsley if you like.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Look for the beef tips and the flavored mashed potatoes in the refrigerated meat and deli case.

rows.title: Buttermilk Syrup
rows.dek: A warm, buttery syrup that turns pancakes and waffles into a treat. Buttermilk, butter and sugar boil together, then a little baking soda makes it foam up high and light. Brown sugar in place of white gives it a deeper caramel taste.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 cup sugar (or brown sugar for a caramel flavor)
steps: Put the butter, sugar, buttermilk, vanilla and corn syrup in a large saucepan, since the syrup foams up a lot.
Bring it to a boil over medium heat, stirring.
Take it off the heat right away and stir in the baking soda.
Let it froth up high. The foam is part of what makes it so good.
Serve it warm over pancakes or waffles.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: For a deeper caramel flavor, use brown sugar in place of the white.

rows.title: Orange-Glazed Coffee Cake
rows.dek: A sweet yeast bread to serve with breakfast: a soft orange and ricotta dough, braided, coiled into a springform pan, brushed with egg and baked golden, then spread with fresh orange icing while still warm.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 package active dry yeast and ¼ cup warm water (105°F to 115°F)
½ cup fresh orange juice and 1 tbsp grated orange zest
Icing, 1 cup confectioners' sugar and 1½ to 2 tbsp fresh orange juice
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water in a large bowl and let it stand until foamy, 5 to 10 minutes. Stir in the milk, orange juice, sugar, ricotta, zest, salt and egg.
With a heavy-duty mixer and paddle on low, beat in 2 cups flour until a wet dough forms, then the rest ½ cup at a time until the dough is stiff.
Knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, 5 to 10 minutes, adding flour as needed.
Put the dough in a greased bowl, turn to coat, cover with a damp cloth and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1½ hours.
Grease a 10-inch springform pan. Punch down the dough, knead 1 to 2 minutes, divide into 3 pieces and roll each into a 20-inch rope.
Braid the ropes, coil the braid in the pan and tuck the ends under. Cover and let rise until almost doubled, 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F, brush with the egg glaze and bake until golden brown, 25 to 30 minutes. Turn out onto a rack, stir the icing smooth, spread it over the warm cake and serve warm.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start about 3½ hours before you want it warm; the two rises take most of that.

rows.title: Almond Streusel Cake
rows.dek: A clipping that turns a plain orange butter cake into something special: a brown sugar and almond streusel baked through the middle and across the top of a tube cake, then a quick orange glaze drizzled over once it cools.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Streusel, 1 cup packed light brown sugar, 1 cup sliced almonds and ¼ cup flour
Plus 3 tbsp melted butter and 1 tsp grated orange zest for the streusel
½ cup (1 stick) butter, softened, and ½ cup granulated sugar
1 tsp grated orange zest and ½ tsp vanilla extract
1 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp baking soda
Glaze, ½ cup confectioners' sugar and 2½ tsp orange juice
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9- or 10-inch tube pan.
For the streusel, mix the brown sugar, almonds and flour, then stir in the melted butter and zest.
Beat the butter and sugar on medium until fluffy, add the eggs one at a time, then beat in the zest and vanilla.
Mix the flour, baking powder and baking soda, and on low speed beat it into the egg mixture alternately with the orange juice, starting and ending with flour.
Spoon in half the batter, sprinkle half the streusel, then top with the rest of the batter and streusel.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean, and cool completely in the pan on a rack.
Turn the cake out right-side up onto a serving plate, stir the glaze smooth and drizzle it over.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: For a different streusel, use chopped walnuts in place of the almonds.

rows.title: Mango Coffee Cake
rows.dek: A prize-winning magazine clipping: a tender buttermilk cake with nutmeg, folded with three cups of chopped mango and topped with cinnamon sugar that bakes into a crackly crust. The mango sinks to the bottom as it bakes. Serve it warm with sweetened whipped cream.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 cups sugar, plus ⅓ cup for the topping
1½ tsp baking powder, ½ tsp baking soda and ¼ tsp salt
1 cup buttermilk or sour milk (1 Tbsp lemon juice or vinegar plus milk to make 1 cup, rested 5 minutes)
3 cups coarsely chopped, seeded and peeled mangoes (about 3)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 13x9x2-inch baking pan.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, the 2 cups sugar, baking powder, baking soda, nutmeg and salt, then cut in the butter with a pastry blender or two knives until it looks like coarse crumbs.
In a small bowl, combine the buttermilk, eggs and vanilla, add it to the flour mixture all at once, and stir just until moistened.
Fold in the mangoes and spread the batter in the pan.
Mix the ⅓ cup sugar with the cinnamon and sprinkle it evenly over the batter.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until a wooden pick near the center comes out clean (break the crust slightly as you insert it); the mango sinks to the bottom.
Cool slightly and serve warm with sweetened whipped cream.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Pineapple Pecan Coffee Cake
rows.dek: A small, old-fashioned square cake from a printed recipe clipping: a plain, tender batter with crushed pineapple, honey, butter and pecans spread on top before baking, so the topping turns glossy and toasty. Best served warm, cut into nine squares.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Topping: 2 Tbsp each softened butter and honey
½ cup well-drained crushed pineapple, for the topping
⅓ cup chopped pecans, for the topping
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease and flour a 9x9x2-inch square pan.
Mix the sugar, shortening and egg thoroughly, then stir in the milk.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together and stir them into the shortening mixture.
Spread the batter in the pan.
Mix the butter, honey, pineapple and pecans and spread the topping over the batter.
Bake 25 to 35 minutes, until done.
Serve warm, cut into 9 squares.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Press the pineapple in a sieve so it's well drained, or the topping runs and the center stays wet.

rows.title: Overnight Coffee Cake
rows.dek: A make-ahead breakfast cake from a magazine clipping: a tender ricotta batter in a 13x9 pan under a crumble of nuts, dark brown sugar, wheat germ, cinnamon and nutmeg. It rests covered in the fridge overnight and bakes in the morning, served warm.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1½ tsp each baking powder and baking soda, plus 1 tsp salt
½ cup packed dark brown sugar
1 Tbsp ground cinnamon and 1 tsp ground nutmeg
steps: Grease the bottom and ½ inch up the sides of a 13x9x2-inch baking pan.
Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a bowl and set it aside.
Beat the butter on medium for 30 seconds, beat in the sugar, then add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each, and beat in the ricotta.
Beat in as much of the flour mixture as you can, stir in the rest with a spoon, and spread the batter in the pan.
Mix the nuts, brown sugar, wheat germ, cinnamon and nutmeg and sprinkle it evenly over the batter. Cover and refrigerate up to 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Uncover and bake 35 to 40 minutes, until a toothpick near the center comes out clean.
Cool slightly in the pan on a wire rack and serve warm.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Assemble it the night before a holiday breakfast and bake it straight from the fridge.

rows.title: Blueberry Buckle Coffee Cake
rows.dek: An oat-batter cake from a newspaper clipping: blueberries tossed with lemon juice and scattered over the batter, then a crumbly oat, cinnamon and nutmeg streusel. It bakes up golden in an 11x7 dish and is best served warm.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Streusel, ½ cup sugar, ½ cup all-purpose flour and ⅓ cup quick or old-fashioned oats
Streusel spices, ½ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp nutmeg
⅓ cup butter or margarine, for the streusel
1 cup quick or old-fashioned oats, uncooked
2½ tsp baking powder and ¼ tsp salt
½ cup butter or margarine and ½ cup sugar
2 cups fresh or frozen blueberries (do not thaw if frozen)
steps: For the streusel, combine the sugar, flour, oats, cinnamon and nutmeg in a medium bowl, cut in the butter until crumbly, and set aside.
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease an 11-by-7-inch baking dish.
In a medium bowl, combine the flour, oats, baking powder and salt and set aside.
In a large bowl, beat the butter and sugar together, then blend in the egg.
Add the flour mixture alternately with the milk, mixing until well blended, and spread it into the dish.
Toss the blueberries with the lemon juice, sprinkle them over the batter, then sprinkle the streusel evenly over the berries.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes and serve warm.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Frozen blueberries go in straight from the freezer; thawing makes them bleed into the batter.

rows.title: Cinnamon Swirl Coffee Cake
rows.dek: A newspaper clipping that dresses up a boxed golden cake mix with sour cream, extra eggs and vanilla, then layers a brown sugar, cinnamon and pecan filling through the middle and across the top. Two round cakes from one bowl, served still a little warm.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Vegetable oil spray and flour, for the pans
1 package (18.5 oz) plain butter recipe golden cake mix
Topping, ½ cup packed light brown sugar and 1 tbsp ground cinnamon
¼ cup finely chopped pecans, optional, for the topping
steps: Set a rack in the center of the oven and heat it to 325°F. Mist two 9-inch metal cake pans (or one 13-by-9-inch pan) with oil spray, dust them with flour and shake out the extra.
Beat the cake mix, sour cream, oil, sugar, eggs and vanilla on low speed for 30 seconds, then scrape down the bowl.
Beat on medium until the batter lightens and is smooth, about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl again if needed.
Divide half the batter between the two pans and smooth the tops. Mix the brown sugar, pecans and cinnamon for the topping.
Spoon half the topping over the batter, pour the rest of the batter over it, and spoon the rest of the topping on top.
Bake the pans side by side 40 to 45 minutes, until golden brown and the tops spring back when lightly pressed.
Cool in the pans on wire racks about 20 minutes, then slice and serve while still a bit warm.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: The pecans are optional; the cinnamon-sugar layer swirls through the cake either way.

rows.title: Holiday Brunch Casserole
rows.dek: A make-ahead brunch: day-old bread and sharp cheddar soaked overnight in a mustard-seasoned egg custard, topped with crumbled sausage, mushrooms and tomatoes, then baked low and slow until puffed and golden.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 package pork breakfast sausage, cooked, drained and crumbled
1 tsp dry mustard, 1 tsp salt and ¼ tsp onion powder
steps: Butter a 9x13 baking dish well and spread the bread cubes in it.
Sprinkle the cheese over the bread.
Whisk the eggs, milk, dry mustard, salt, onion powder and pepper, and pour it evenly over the bread and cheese.
Scatter the sausage, and the mushrooms and tomatoes if using, over the top.
Cover and chill overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F and bake uncovered for about 1 hour, until puffed and set.
If the top browns too quickly, tent it loosely with foil.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Assemble it the night before, so the morning is just one hour in the oven.

rows.title: Sour Cream Coffee Cake
rows.dek: A small-pan clipping cake: a rich sour cream butter cake baked in an 8-inch square pan, with cinnamon-sugar streusel layered through the middle and scattered over the top. Let it cool before cutting, and eat it fresh or freeze it the same day.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Streusel, 3 tbsp firmly packed brown sugar, ½ cup granulated sugar and ½ tsp ground cinnamon
1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp baking powder and ¼ tsp salt
steps: For the streusel, stir together the brown sugar, granulated sugar and cinnamon, then cut in the 2 tbsp butter with a pastry blender or 2 knives until crumbly; set aside.
Heat the oven to 325°F and grease and flour an 8-inch square baking pan.
Cream the ½ cup butter and the sugar in an electric mixer until light and creamy, then beat in the eggs.
Stir together the flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt, add it to the butter mixture alternately with the sour cream, then stir in the vanilla.
Pour half the batter into the pan, sprinkle on half the streusel, top with the rest of the batter and sprinkle on the remaining streusel.
Bake until the cake is firm to the touch and a wooden pick in the center comes out clean, 45 to 50 minutes.
Cool 30 minutes before cutting into 9 squares; cut sooner and it is very crumbly.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Eat it or freeze it the day it is made; to serve, thaw and reheat at 325°F for 10 minutes.

rows.title: German Pancakes
rows.dek: A whole-pan German pancake: eggs, milk and flour whizzed in the blender, poured over melted butter and baked hot until it puffs up high with golden edges. Cut it in squares and finish with lemon juice and powdered sugar, or fresh fruit.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Fresh lemon juice and powdered sugar, or fresh fruit, for topping
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F, melt the butter in a 9-by-13-inch pan, and set it aside.
In a blender, mix the eggs, milk, flour and salt until smooth.
Pour the batter over the melted butter.
Bake 20 to 30 minutes, until puffed high and golden at the edges.
Cut into squares and top lightly with fresh lemon juice and powdered sugar, or with fresh fruit.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Melt the butter in the pan while the oven heats, so the batter hits hot butter and puffs higher.

rows.title: Bagel, Lox and Egg Strata
rows.dek: A make-ahead brunch bake: bite-size bagel pieces layered with smoked salmon, Swiss cheese and chives, soaked overnight in an egg and cottage cheese custard, then baked until puffed and golden.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 4 to 6 plain bagels, cut into bite-size pieces (8 cups)
1 package (3 oz) thinly sliced smoked salmon (lox-style), cut into small pieces
8 oz Swiss or Monterey Jack cheese, shredded (2 cups)
steps: Spread the melted butter over the bottom of a 3-quart rectangular baking dish.
Spread the bagel pieces evenly in the dish, then sprinkle the lox, cheese and chives over them.
In a large bowl beat the eggs, then stir in the milk, cottage cheese and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over the layers and press down gently with the back of a wooden spoon until everything is moistened.
Cover and chill for 4 to 24 hours.
Bake uncovered at 350°F for about 45 minutes, until the center is set and the edges are puffed and golden.
Let it stand 10 minutes before cutting into 12 squares.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Assemble it the night before and bake it in the morning.

rows.title: Apple Pancakes
rows.dek: Finely diced apple tossed in cinnamon, nutmeg and sugar, then folded into plain buttermilk pancake batter. They come off the griddle small and golden with soft, spiced apple in every bite. Butter and syrup on top.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Butter or your favorite syrup, for serving
steps: In a small bowl, mix the cinnamon, nutmeg and sugar.
Add the diced apples and toss until they are coated completely.
In a medium bowl, mix the pancake mix and water the usual way.
Stir in the apple mixture.
Fry the pancakes on a hot greased griddle as usual, about four inches across, turning once when bubbles form.
Serve with butter or your favorite syrup.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Dice the apple small so it cooks through before the pancake browns.

rows.title: Cranberry Pancakes
rows.dek: A day-after-Thanksgiving breakfast: buttermilk pancake mix stirred with a little canned cranberry sauce, so the pancakes come out pink and tart, then the rest of the sauce warmed with corn syrup into a quick ruby syrup to pour over the stack.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: In a medium bowl, mix the pancake mix, water and ½ cup of the cranberry sauce.
Fry the pancakes on a hot griddle in the usual way and keep them warm.
In a small saucepan, heat the rest of the cranberry sauce with the corn syrup until smooth and warm.
Serve the sauce over the pancakes. Makes about 12 pancakes and 1 cup of sauce.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: A good way to use up leftover cranberry sauce the morning after Thanksgiving.

rows.title: Pineapple Waffles
rows.dek: A waffle: buttermilk pancake mix stirred with oil and the juice from a can of crushed pineapple, then the fruit folded in. Baked crisp in the waffle iron and served with ham or sausage, sweet and salty together.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 cup liquid from drained canned pineapple
steps: Drain the can of crushed pineapple over a measuring cup, saving 1 cup of the juice.
In a medium bowl, combine the pancake mix, oil and pineapple juice.
Stir in the crushed pineapple.
Cook in a hot waffle iron following the manufacturer's directions.
Serve with ham or sausage. Makes 6 to 7 seven-inch waffles.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: If the can gives less than a cup of juice, top it up with water.

rows.title: Spicy Surprise Waffles
rows.dek: Plain buttermilk pancake mix turned into a fall breakfast with cinnamon, nutmeg and a dash each of cloves and allspice. Bake in the waffle iron and serve with butter, applesauce or apple butter.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Butter, applesauce or apple butter, for serving
steps: Heat the waffle iron.
In a medium bowl, combine the pancake mix, oil, water, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves and allspice and blend well.
Bake the batter in the waffle iron according to the maker's directions.
Serve with butter, applesauce or apple butter. Makes about five 5-inch waffles.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Any buttermilk pancake mix works; warm the applesauce for a cold morning.

rows.title: Sourdough Pancakes
rows.dek: A pancake that starts a week early: a sourdough starter stirred daily, then a cup of it folded into buttermilk pancake mix. The batter rests fifteen minutes and fries up tangy and light.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Starter: 2 packages (¼ oz each) active dry yeast
Equal parts flour and water, to feed the starter
steps: For the starter, mix the flour, warm water, yeast and sugar in a glass jar or crock with a loose-fitting lid.
Cover with a clean towel or cheesecloth and let it stand in a warm place (80°F to 90°F) for 5 to 7 days, stirring it down daily.
For the pancakes, mix the pancake mix, water and 1 cup of starter in a medium bowl.
Let the batter rest at least 15 minutes, then fry on a hot griddle as usual.
To keep the starter going, replace what you took out with equal parts water and flour (1 cup of each), cover loosely and leave it at room temperature overnight.
Put the lid on and refrigerate the starter; let it stand at room temperature at least 1 hour before using.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start the starter a week before a pancake weekend; once it is going, one cup and a box of mix make breakfast for a crowd.

rows.title: Potato Pancakes
rows.dek: A savory griddle pancake: buttermilk pancake batter with grated potato and a little onion stirred in, plus green pepper, pimiento, parsley or ham if you like. Fried golden and served with applesauce.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 cups grated raw potato, or frozen O'Brien or hash brown potatoes, thawed
Chopped green pepper, pimiento, parsley or diced ham, to taste (optional)
steps: In a medium bowl, combine the pancake mix, salt, water and beaten eggs as for regular pancakes.
Mix in the potatoes, onion and any of the optional add-ins.
Fry on a hot greased griddle as you would regular pancakes, turning once, until golden brown on both sides.
Serve hot with applesauce.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Pat thawed frozen potatoes dry before mixing so the pancakes crisp at the edges.

rows.title: Hamburger Soup
rows.dek: A thick, old-fashioned soup from one pot: browned hamburger, cabbage, carrots, celery and tomatoes simmered in beef broth with a little rice, thyme, basil and a touch of brown sugar. Serve it with crusty bread.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 cup chopped onion and ½ cup chopped celery
3 beef bouillon cubes dissolved in 2 quarts water
1 small bay leaf and 2 tbsp brown sugar
½ tsp thyme, 1 tsp basil, 1 tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper
steps: Brown the hamburger in a soup pot.
Dissolve the bouillon cubes in the 2 quarts of water.
Mix all the other ingredients and the broth into the hamburger.
Cook on medium high until the vegetables are tender.
Remove the bay leaf when the soup is ready. It should be thick.
Serve hot with crusty bread.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Use regular white rice, not instant, so it holds up in the pot; the soup thickens as it sits.

rows.title: Black Bean Soup
rows.dek: A big pot of black bean soup: dry beans simmered with celery, onion, green pepper, carrots, garlic and a warm mix of basil, oregano, cumin and cayenne, then finished with tomatoes and white corn. Eighteen cups, enough to share or freeze.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 3 cups dry black beans, soaked and drained
1 cup each chopped celery, chopped onion and chopped green bell pepper
1 cup sliced carrots and 4 cloves garlic, minced
2 tsp dried basil and 2 tsp dried oregano
1 tsp black pepper, ½ tsp ground cumin and ¼ tsp cayenne
2 cans (15 oz) whole tomatoes, undrained and chopped
steps: Soak the beans in water to cover overnight, or boil them 2 minutes and let them stand 1 hour, then drain.
Place the beans in a large stockpot with the water, salt, celery, onion, bell pepper, carrot, garlic, basil, oregano, pepper, cumin, cayenne and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat and simmer 1½ hours, until the beans are tender.
Add the tomatoes, corn and tomato sauce and stir well.
Bring back to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, uncovered, 30 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: The soup freezes well in portions.

rows.title: Spiced Apple and Butternut Squash Soup
rows.dek: A big pot of fall soup: tart Granny Smith apples and onions softened in butter, warmed with nutmeg, allspice and cinnamon, then simmered with butternut squash and stock and puréed smooth.
rows.image_alt: Spiced Apple and Butternut Squash Soup
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 large Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored and diced
4 butternut squashes, peeled, halved lengthwise, seeded and cut in 1-inch cubes
3 quarts chicken stock, plus more if needed
Salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and apples and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the nutmeg, allspice and cinnamon and cook for 1 minute.
Add the squash and chicken stock and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer, uncovered, until the squash is tender, 20 to 30 minutes.
Purée the soup, adding more stock if needed to reach the thickness you like.
Season with salt and pepper and serve. Refrigerate any leftovers.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: An immersion blender purées it right in the pot, and pre-cubed squash skips the peeling.

rows.title: Chicken Tortilla Spinach Casserole
rows.dek: A layered Mexican-style casserole: corn tortillas, shredded chicken, black beans, spinach and green-chile tomatoes in a creamy cumin and smoked paprika sauce, baked under melted cheese. Top it with tomato, avocado, lettuce and salsa.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 large onion, diced, and 2 cloves garlic, minced
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (10 oz) diced tomatoes with green chiles
1 cup chicken broth and 1 cup sour cream
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, ½ tsp smoked paprika, salt and pepper to taste
Tomato, avocado, shredded lettuce and salsa, to top
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 baking dish.
Sauté the onion until soft, add the garlic for a minute, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.
In a large bowl, mix the onion and spinach with the chicken, beans, tomatoes, spices, broth and sour cream; season with salt and pepper.
Line the dish with a layer of tortillas, spread on part of the filling and sprinkle with cheese.
Repeat two or three times, ending with cheese on top.
Bake covered about 25 minutes, then uncovered about 10 minutes, until hot and bubbly.
Let it rest a few minutes, then top with tomato, avocado, shredded lettuce and salsa.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Add the toppings after baking, never before.

rows.title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
rows.dek: A light weeknight soup: chicken simmered in broth with a little rice, carrot and onion, then finished with tomato, fresh cilantro and green taco sauce. The fun is at the table, where everyone adds tortilla chips, cheese and avocado or guacamole.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 small bunch cilantro, stems cut off, chopped
Tortilla chips and cheese, to serve
steps: Boil the chicken breasts in the chicken broth until cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Lift the chicken out of the broth and chop it.
Add the rice, carrot and onion to the broth, reduce the heat, and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Add the chopped chicken, tomato, cilantro and green taco sauce, and simmer another 5 minutes.
Serve with tortilla chips and cheese, plus avocados or guacamole.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start with 2 tbsp of green taco sauce and add more at the end if you want more heat.

rows.title: Navy Bean and Ham Soup
rows.dek: A holiday ham bone, a pound of dry navy beans, carrots, celery and onion go into the pressure cooker with water and no soaking. Ninety minutes later the meat has fallen off the bone into a thick, meaty soup that tastes even better as leftovers.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 meaty ham bone (or extra loose ham)
1 lb dry navy beans, not soaked
¼ tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper
steps: Put the ham bone and the dry beans in the pressure cooker first.
Sprinkle the onion, celery, carrots, bay leaf, salt and pepper around them, then pour in the water last.
Lock the lid with the valve closed and cook on High pressure for 90 minutes.
Release the pressure when the cooking is done.
Pull out the ham bone; it comes out clean because the meat has already fallen off into the soup.
Take out the bay leaf and serve hot.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: It gets better each day as leftovers, so it is the best use for the ham bone after a holiday dinner.

rows.title: Baked Potato Soup
rows.dek: A soup for a cold night: baked potatoes scooped into a thick butter-and-milk base with cheddar, crumbled bacon and green onions, and sour cream stirred in at the end. Add the milk a little at a time, stir constantly, and never let it boil.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ¾ tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper
4 green onions, chopped, green part too
steps: Wash the potatoes, prick them several times with a fork, and bake at 400°F for 1 hour or until done. Let them cool.
Cut the potatoes in half lengthwise, scoop out and save the pulp, and throw away the shells.
Melt the butter in a big, deep pan over low heat. Add the flour and stir until smooth, then cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the milk gradually, 3 cups first and then 1 cup at a time as it thickens. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick and bubbly.
Stir in the potato, salt, pepper, cheese, bacon and green onions, plus the clams if you use them. Cook until heated through, but do not let it boil.
Five minutes before serving, stir in the sour cream.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Add the milk a little at a time, keep stirring, and never let it boil once the cheese is in.

rows.title: Turkey-Vegetable Soup
rows.dek: A quick soup for the day after the feast: leftover roast turkey with fennel, carrots, garlic and escarole in chicken broth, with cannellini beans, some mashed to give the broth body. Light, high in fiber and ready in 30 minutes.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 carton (32 oz) lower-sodium chicken broth and 1 cup water
1 bulb fennel (14 oz), trimmed, cored and chopped
¼ tsp each salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 small head escarole (7 oz), thinly sliced
1 can (15 to 19 oz) cannellini beans, rinsed and drained, ½ cup of them mashed
steps: Put the broth and 1 cup of water in a large microwave-safe bowl, cover with vented plastic wrap and microwave on High for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a 6-quart pot on medium until hot.
