Add the fennel, carrots, garlic, salt and pepper and cook 8 minutes, stirring often, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the escarole and cook 3 minutes, stirring often, until wilted.
Add the mashed and whole beans and the hot broth, bring to a boil on high, then reduce to medium and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the turkey and heat through, about 1 minute.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: No microwave needed; heat the broth and water in a second pot while the vegetables cook.

rows.title: Clam Chowder
rows.dek: A restaurant-style chowder scaled for a crowd: bacon, onion and celery, a long-cooked butter-and-flour base thinned with clam juice, then potatoes, chopped clams and half-and-half. Thick, briny and rich. Heat it gently at the end and never let it boil.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1½ cups diced onion and 2¾ cups diced celery (4 ribs)
½ tsp minced fresh garlic and ½ tsp dried leaf thyme
1 tsp dry mustard and ¼ tsp black pepper
1 (51 oz) can chopped sea clams, with juice
steps: In a 1½-gallon pot, brown the bacon. Add the onion and celery and sauté until translucent.
Add the butter, garlic, thyme, mustard and pepper, and mix thoroughly.
Add the flour and mix well, then cook about 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Strain the juice from the chopped clams and set the clams aside. Add the can of clam juice and the strained juice to the pot.
Simmer about 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer 20 to 30 minutes, until tender.
Stir in the chopped clams and half-and-half and heat to serving temperature, but do not let it boil.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Makes a full gallon; to freeze some, take it out before the half-and-half goes in and add the cream when you reheat.

rows.title: Chicken Corn Chowder
rows.dek: A weeknight chowder: bacon crisped first, onion and green chiles softened in the drippings, then broth, potatoes and corn, with diced chicken and half-and-half stirred in at the end. Mild, creamy and a little smoky, with the bacon crumbled on top.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 4 or 5 red or yellow potatoes, chopped
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp, lift it out and crumble it.
In the bacon drippings, sauté the onion and green chiles until soft, then stir in the thyme.
Add the chicken broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and corn, bring to a boil and cook 10 minutes, or until the potatoes are soft.
Add the chicken and half-and-half and heat until hot.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with the bacon crumbled on top.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Six cups of broth makes a looser chowder, four a thicker one; leftover or rotisserie chicken works for the cooked breasts.

rows.title: Harvest Vegetable Soup
rows.dek: A big-pot soup for late summer and fall, when the garden is full: zucchini, potatoes, carrots, green beans, broccoli, peppers, sweet corn and ripe tomatoes simmered in vegetable juice with fresh basil, parsley and oregano, and alphabet pasta for the kids.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 4 medium zucchini, 6 medium potatoes and 6 medium carrots
1 cup green beans, chopped, and 1 cup broccoli
4 ears corn, kernels cut from the cob
6 cups water, plus more if needed
1 tbsp each fresh basil, parsley and oregano, chopped
6 oz dried pasta (such as alphabet noodles), uncooked
steps: Wash and cut the zucchini, potatoes, carrots, green beans, broccoli, green peppers, corn and tomatoes.
Put the vegetables in a large cooking pot and add enough water to cover them, starting with 6 cups.
Add the vegetable juice and toss in the fresh basil, parsley and oregano.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
About 10 minutes before eating, add the pasta.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: It makes a huge pot, so use the biggest stockpot you have or halve it.

rows.title: Taco Soup with Toppings Bar
rows.dek: A quick pot of beef, kidney beans, stewed tomatoes and corn simmered with taco seasoning, served over a layer of corn chips. The fun is the toppings bar: lettuce, avocado, cheddar, olives, sour cream and tomatoes in bowls so everyone builds their own.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can corn, or about 1½ cups frozen corn
Toppings: shredded lettuce, chopped avocado, grated cheddar cheese, olives, sour cream, chopped tomatoes
Corn chips, for the bottom of each bowl
steps: In a heavy saucepan or Dutch oven, cook the ground beef and onion until the meat is brown and no longer pink.
Drain off the fat.
Add the water, stewed tomatoes, corn, kidney beans with their liquid, tomato sauce and taco seasoning mix.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, set out each topping in its own bowl.
Place a layer of corn chips in the bottom of each soup bowl, ladle the soup over them, and let everyone top their bowl as they like.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Canned or frozen corn both work, added with the stewed tomatoes.

rows.title: Butternut Squash and Roasted Red Pepper Soup
rows.dek: A fall soup: broiled red peppers puréed and simmered with butternut squash, onion, cumin and coriander, then blended smooth and warmed with cayenne and nutmeg. Served with diced tomatoes, toasted cashews and, if you like, a dollop of crème fraîche.
rows.image_alt: Butternut Squash and Roasted Red Pepper Soup
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 red bell peppers, seeded, cored and halved lengthwise
2 Tbsp canola oil plus 1 Tbsp butter
1 tsp each ground cumin and ground coriander
3 lb butternut squash (about 2 large), peeled, seeded and cubed
⅛ tsp cayenne, ¼ tsp nutmeg and ¼ tsp black pepper
Crème fraîche, for a dollop on top (optional)
Diced tomatoes and toasted cashews, to serve
steps: Broil the peppers skin side up on a foil-lined baking sheet with the oven door slightly ajar until black blisters form, 8 to 10 minutes.
Cool the peppers 20 minutes, purée them in a blender until smooth and set aside.
Heat the butter and oil in a heavy stockpot over medium-high heat and cook the onion, stirring often, until soft but not browned, about 4 minutes.
Add the cumin and coriander and cook 1 more minute.
Add the squash, water, pepper purée and salt, cover, and simmer over low heat until the squash is very soft, 35 to 40 minutes.
Purée the soup with an immersion blender, or in batches in a blender, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the cayenne, nutmeg and black pepper, and serve topped with diced tomatoes, toasted cashews and a dollop of crème fraîche if you like.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card

rows.title: Fabulous French Toast
rows.dek: The secret is a little flour and evaporated milk in the egg mixture, so thick slices fry up golden and crisp outside and custardy inside. A quick soak, a touch of butter in a hot pan, and about 90 seconds a side.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ⅓ cup sugar (more or less to taste)
A dash of cinnamon, if you like
steps: Whisk the eggs, evaporated milk, flour, sugar, vanilla, salt and cinnamon together until smooth.
Heat the pan until it is hot, then spread a touch of butter on it. If the butter smokes, the pan is too hot.
Soak each slice of bread in the egg mixture, but don't let it get soggy.
Place the slices in the pan and cook each side about 90 seconds, or until golden and done.
Add a touch more butter to the pan between batches and serve hot.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Makes 6 thick slices, about 2 per person; adjust the sugar to your taste.

rows.title: Western Cubed Potatoes
rows.dek: An easy oven side: cubed potatoes tossed in melted butter with mild green chiles, a little onion and garlic salt, baked covered until soft, then uncovered to finish, and showered with fresh parsley.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ½ cup butter or margarine, melted
steps: In a large bowl, combine the butter, green chiles, onion, salt, garlic salt and pepper.
Add the potatoes and toss to coat.
Transfer to an ungreased 2-quart baking dish.
Cover and bake at 350°F for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake 20 to 25 minutes longer, until the potatoes are tender.
Sprinkle with the parsley and serve.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Butter or margarine both work.

rows.title: Hashed Brown Potatoes
rows.dek: The simplest diner side: small potato cubes steamed under a lid in plenty of butter, then uncovered, seasoned with paprika and pepper, and turned over high heat until golden and crisp.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 6 medium potatoes, peeled and finely cubed (about 5 cups)
steps: Heat the butter in a 10-inch skillet.
Add the potatoes, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Uncover, add the salt, paprika and pepper, and mix well.
Keep cooking over fairly high heat, turning the potatoes with a spatula as they brown, until they are tender and crisp.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Cut the cubes small and even, about ½ inch, so they cook through under the lid and crisp at the same time.

rows.title: Swedish Waffles
rows.dek: Thin, tender waffles: just a cup of flour carried by buttermilk, four eggs and a stick of melted butter. The batter pours almost like cream, and the waffles bake light and crisp-edged. Take them out when the iron stops steaming.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Heat the waffle iron.
Sift the flour, salt, baking soda and baking powder together into a bowl.
Add the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter to the flour mixture and stir just until blended. The batter will be thin.
Pour batter into the hot waffle iron and close it.
When it stops steaming or the indicator light comes on, take the waffle out.
Repeat with the rest of the batter. Makes about six 4-square waffles.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: The batter is meant to be thin, so don't add flour; it is what makes these light and tender.

rows.title: Red Pepper Dip
rows.dek: A warm baked dip: roasted red peppers and artichoke hearts folded into Parmesan and mayonnaise with butter-softened green onions, baked in a pie pan until bubbly and finished with parsley and more Parmesan. Serve it hot with crackers.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 (7 oz) jar roasted red peppers, or 1 cup, cut up
1 (8 oz) can artichoke hearts (not marinated), drained and cut up
1 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for the top
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Sauté the green onions in the butter until soft.
Mix the green onions, red peppers, artichoke hearts, pepper, Parmesan and mayonnaise.
Spread the mixture in a 9-inch pie pan and sprinkle parsley and more Parmesan over the top.
Bake 20 minutes, until hot and bubbly, and serve warm with crackers.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Use regular mayonnaise and plain artichoke hearts; fat-free mayo and marinated hearts change the dip.

rows.title: Layered Taco Appetizer Pizza
rows.dek: A party wedge: a baked pie crust spread with taco-seasoned refried beans, a ring of guacamole, a creamy salsa center and a scatter of olives, green chiles and green onions. It is made ahead and served cold, cut like a pizza.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 refrigerated pie crust (from a 15 oz package)
1 can (2.5 oz) ripe olives, sliced or chopped, drained
1 can (4 oz) diced green chiles, drained
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F. Place the crust on a 12-inch pizza pan or cookie sheet, flute the edge and prick it all over with a fork.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until golden brown, and let it cool.
Mix the beans and taco seasoning and spread them on the crust to within ½ inch of the edge.
Spoon the guacamole in a circle on the beans about 1½ inches from the edge and gently spread it into a 2-inch ring.
Mix the cream cheese with 2 tablespoons of the salsa and spoon it into the middle of the ring.
Garnish the ring with the rest of the salsa, the olives, green chiles, green onions and cheese if you like.
Cover and refrigerate until serving, then cut into wedges.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Make it ahead; it holds covered in the fridge until the party starts.

rows.title: Spiced Russian Cider
rows.dek: Despite the name, there is no apple in it: orange and lemon juice simmered with cinnamon, cloves, vanilla and almond until the whole house smells like the holidays. A big pot keeps warm on the stove for a crowd.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Boil 2 cups of water and the sugar together for 5 minutes.
Add the orange juice, lemon juice, 2 quarts of water, vanilla, almond extract, cinnamon sticks and cloves.
Heat to boiling, then turn the burner down and simmer 30 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon sticks and cloves and serve hot.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Use 1¼ cups sugar, or 2 cups for a sweeter punch.

rows.title: Mini Comté and Mushroom Burgers
rows.dek: Small burgers with a grown-up topping: onions cooked slowly until sweet and golden, buttery browned mushrooms, and a thick slice of nutty Comté melted under the broiler. Brioche buns keep them soft and a little rich; lettuce and tomato freshen each bite.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 8 two-inch brioche buns or dinner rolls, halved and toasted
8 slices Comté cheese, about ¼ inch thick
Lettuce and tomato slices, for serving
steps: Cook the onion in the olive oil in a medium skillet over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden brown and caramelized.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet and cook the mushrooms until browned; season with salt and pepper.
Shape the beef into 8 small patties and season them with salt and pepper.
Cook the patties on both sides to the doneness you like.
Move the burgers to a baking sheet, top each with a spoonful of mushrooms and a slice of Comté, and broil just until the cheese melts.
Serve on the toasted buns with the onions, lettuce and tomato.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Heat the broiler while the patties cook so the cheese melts the moment they come off the stove.

rows.title: Tuscan Chicken Skillet
rows.dek: A one-pan weeknight supper: chicken tenderloins seared in olive oil, then simmered in fire-roasted tomatoes with mushrooms, sun-dried tomatoes, cannellini beans, garlic, oregano and thyme, and finished with a handful of fresh parsley.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast tenderloins, 2 Tbsp olive oil
½ cup chopped yellow onion and 3 cloves garlic, minced
1 can (14.5 oz) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 tsp oregano and ½ tsp thyme
1 tsp kosher salt, ½ tsp fresh-ground black pepper, plus salt and pepper for the chicken
steps: Season the tenderloins with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear them 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden, then set them on a plate.
In the same skillet, cook the onion and mushrooms 5 to 6 minutes, until the mushrooms brown, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the fire-roasted tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes, cannellini beans, oregano, thyme, sugar, kosher salt and black pepper.
Bring it to a simmer and cook 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens a little.
Nestle the chicken back into the sauce, cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (165°F).
Scatter the chopped parsley over the top and serve from the skillet.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Just one teaspoon of sugar softens the tomatoes.

rows.title: Yogurt-Curry Marinated Chicken Thighs
rows.dek: Weeknight chicken: boneless thighs soaked half a day in yogurt, grated onion and curry powder, then grilled or broiled until browned at the edges. The yogurt keeps the meat tender, and a pinch of crushed red pepper gives it a little heat.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 4 large or 8 small boneless chicken thighs
steps: Whisk the yogurt, onion, curry powder, olive oil, salt and crushed red pepper together in a shallow pan.
Add the chicken and turn it until it is well coated.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, and up to 8.
Heat the grill to medium-high or the broiler to high.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade and throw the marinade away.
Grill or broil, turning once or twice, until the chicken is no longer pink in the middle, 25 to 30 minutes, and serve.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: No grill? The broiler on high does the same job; start the marinade in the morning for dinner.

rows.title: Smoked Jerk Chicken
rows.dek: Chicken soaks in a blended marinade of orange, lime, allspice, cinnamon, thyme, garlic, scallions and habanero, then slow-smokes on an ordinary grill set up for indirect heat with a pan of wood chips. It comes out spicy, citrusy and a little sweet.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Zest and juice of 1 orange and 1 lime
2 tsp each cinnamon, allspice and thyme
1 Tbsp soy sauce, 2 tsp sugar and 1 Tbsp kosher salt
5 to 6 lb bone-in chicken thighs, drumsticks and breasts
steps: Zest the orange and lime, then juice them. Blend the zest and juice with the cinnamon, allspice, thyme, garlic, scallions, soy sauce, sugar, salt, habaneros and olive oil until smooth.
Divide the marinade and chicken between 2 zip-top bags and refrigerate 3 to 24 hours.
Light one side of a gas grill to medium, or set up a charcoal grill for indirect grilling at 250 to 300°F. Set a foil pan with ½ cup wood chips over the heat.
Grill the chicken skin side up on oiled grates on the side away from the heat. Close the lid and leave it undisturbed for 30 minutes.
Add the other ½ cup wood chips to the pan and flip the chicken. Add charcoal or adjust the burners to hold the temperature.
After 1 hour, check with an instant-read thermometer. Breasts are done at 165°F, thighs and drumsticks at 180°F. This takes 1 to 2 hours or more, and breasts may finish first.
Refrigerate any leftovers.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start with one habanero for a milder batch, and blend the marinade the night before.

rows.title: Crispy Chicken Thighs Stuffed with Ham and Parmesan
rows.dek: Boneless thighs pounded thin, wrapped around a little ham, Parmesan, sage and garlic, then dipped in egg white and rolled in breadcrumbs. They bake crisp in under 20 minutes, so it works on a weeknight.
rows.image_alt: Crispy Chicken Thighs Stuffed with Ham and Parmesan
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 8 boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 1½ lb), trimmed of fat
½ cup chopped flavorful ham or smoked turkey
¼ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
1 Tbsp chopped fresh sage or 1 tsp dried (optional)
½ cup fine dry unseasoned breadcrumbs
½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp ground black pepper
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Lay the thighs smooth side down between two pieces of plastic wrap and pound them gently with a heavy skillet or rolling pin to flatten them slightly.
In a small bowl, stir together the ham or smoked turkey, Parmesan, sage and garlic.
In a second small bowl, whisk the egg whites until frothy. In a third, mix the breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
Put about 1½ tablespoons of filling in the center of each thigh, bring the sides up to meet in the middle, and secure with a toothpick.
Dip each stuffed thigh in the egg whites, then roll it in the breadcrumbs.
Set them seam side down on a baking sheet, drizzle with the olive oil, and bake 15 to 20 minutes, until golden and cooked through to 165°F.
Remove the toothpicks before serving.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Smoked turkey works just as well as ham in the filling, and the sage can be left out.

rows.title: Italian Slow Cooker Chicken
rows.dek: A five-minute morning job: potatoes and carrots in the slow cooker, chicken on top, a whole bottle of Italian dressing poured over, and a shower of herbs and Parmesan. By supper it is a full meal in one pot.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, or 6 thighs
4 to 6 big potatoes, scrubbed and cut in halves or wedges (peeled if you like)
steps: Put the potatoes and carrots in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Lay the chicken on top of the vegetables.
Pour the whole bottle of Italian dressing over the chicken and vegetables.
Sprinkle with Italian seasoning and the grated Parmesan.
Cover and cook on Low 6 to 8 hours or High 3 to 4 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the potatoes are tender.
Serve the chicken with the potatoes, carrots and a spoonful of the juices.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Thighs stay juicier over a long cook on Low.

rows.title: Crescent Chicken Roll-Ups
rows.dek: A cozy weeknight bake: shredded chicken, cream cheese and mozzarella rolled up in crescent dough, set in a creamy chicken sauce and baked golden with Parmesan on top. Pour the sauce around the rolls, never over, so they stay crisp.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 tsp instant minced onion and ¼ tsp garlic powder
½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper
¼ cup grated Parmesan or Romano
1 can (10.75 oz) cream of chicken soup
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and lightly spray an 11x7 baking dish.
In a medium bowl, mix the chicken, cream cheese, minced onion, garlic powder, salt, pepper and mozzarella, plus the bacon if using. Set aside.
In another bowl, stir the milk into the soup a little at a time until smooth.
Separate the dough into 8 triangles. Place about ¼ cup filling on the wide end of each, roll it up and seal it completely.
Set the rolls in the dish in 2 rows of 4, leaving space on all sides for the sauce.
Pour the sauce around the rolls, not over them, or they'll be soggy. Sprinkle the tops with Parmesan or Romano.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until nicely browned.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Toss some cooked bacon into the filling if you like.

rows.title: Cold Sesame Pasta with Chicken and Vegetables
rows.dek: A summer potluck salad: spiral pasta, crisp peppers, broccoli, carrots, snow peas, water chestnuts and strips of chicken, all coated in a rich sesame-soy dressing with a little heat and finished with toasted sesame seeds.
rows.image_alt: Cold Sesame Pasta with Chicken and Vegetables
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 lb fusilli, or other pasta, plus a little oil
1 small each green, red and yellow pepper, chopped or shredded (about ¼ cup each)
1 cup broccoli florets and 1 cup julienned snow peas, blanched
¾ cup shredded raw carrots (2 small)
½ lb white chicken meat, grilled or baked, in thin strips
Sauce: 1 cup sesame paste or peanut butter, 6 Tbsp sesame oil, ¼ cup soy oil
½ cup soy sauce and 6 Tbsp rice vinegar
steps: Boil the fusilli until al dente, drain, rinse in cold water and toss in a large bowl with a little oil.
Mix in the green, red and yellow peppers, broccoli, carrots, snow peas, water chestnuts and chicken.
In a blender or food processor, blend the sesame paste, sesame oil and soy oil until smooth.
With the machine running, pour in the soy sauce, vinegar and crushed red pepper, and blend until smooth.
Pour a cup of the sauce over the salad and mix well, then add more in small amounts until everything is well coated. Refrigerate any leftover dressing for later.
Sprinkle with the toasted sesame seeds. Serve chilled, but not straight from the refrigerator.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Leave out the chicken, or swap in shrimp or other vegetables; the salad won't suffer.

rows.title: Southern-Style Fried Chicken
rows.dek: A homemade take on a famous fried chicken. A tangy lemon and herb paste soaks in for hours, then a pancake-mix coating with paprika and sage is fried quickly and finished in the oven, covered until tender and uncovered until crisp.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 3 lb chicken parts, cut into small pieces
2 (0.6 oz) packages Italian salad dressing mix
1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp ground sage and ¼ tsp pepper
steps: Wipe the chicken dry.
Mix the dressing mix, flour, lemon juice, salt and butter into a paste, coat the chicken evenly, stack it in a bowl and refrigerate several hours.
Mix the pancake mix with the paprika, sage and pepper.
Dip each piece in the milk, then in the pancake mixture, and dust off the excess.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and fry the chicken until lightly browned, about 4 minutes a side.
Lay the chicken in a shallow baking pan, spoon the remaining milk over it and seal with foil.
Bake at 350°F for 1 hour, then uncover and bake 20 minutes at 400°F to crisp.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start the paste in the morning so the chicken has hours to soak before supper.

rows.title: Sesame Chicken Salad with Ginger Dressing
rows.dek: A quick main-dish salad: chicken breasts pressed in sesame seeds and browned in a hot pan, sliced thin over crisp greens, and finished with a warm ginger, soy and honey dressing with a little heat from red pepper flakes.
rows.image_alt: Sesame Chicken Salad with Ginger Dressing
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 chicken breasts (about 1 lb) and 3 Tbsp sesame seeds
steps: Press the sesame seeds onto both sides of the chicken breasts.
Heat the oil in a skillet, or spray it with cooking spray, over medium heat.
Sizzle the chicken until both sides are browned and the center reaches 165°F, then let it rest a few minutes.
For the dressing, stir the vinegar, soy sauce, honey, ginger, mustard oil, sesame oil and red pepper flakes in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, and remove from the heat.
Slice the chicken thinly and lay it over a bed of lettuce greens.
Drizzle the warm dressing over the salad and serve.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: No mustard oil on hand? Whisk in ¼ tsp prepared mustard instead.

rows.title: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole
rows.dek: Chicken cordon bleu turned into a layered bake: chicken, bacon, ham and Swiss cheese under a creamy sauce of chicken soup and sour cream. No rolling, no breading, and it all spoons over rice.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F.
Cut the chicken, bacon, Canadian bacon or ham, and cheese into strips or chunks.
Layer them in a casserole dish in this order, chicken, then bacon, then Canadian bacon or ham, then cheese.
Mix the cream of chicken soup and sour cream and spread the sauce over the top.
Bake 30 to 45 minutes.
Serve over rice.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Cut the chicken in small, even chunks and bake until it reaches 165°F; the bacon goes in raw, so lay it in small pieces.

rows.title: Lime Chicken Enchiladas
rows.dek: Chicken poached with garlic, oregano and lime, rolled in softened corn tortillas and baked under a tangy lime sour cream sauce with cheddar. Bright, creamy and mild, with a broth to keep for another day.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 (3½ to 4 lb) chicken, cut into pieces
1 cup diced onion and 2½ Tbsp chopped garlic
1 cup chicken broth plus 1 tsp lime juice
2 tsp white pepper and 2 tsp dried oregano
Juice of 2½ limes, divided, and the grated peel of 1 lime (green part only)
1 (16 oz) container sour cream, ½ cup half-and-half and a pinch of cayenne
Vegetable oil, for softening the tortillas
steps: Put the chicken, onion, broth, the 1 tsp lime juice, garlic, white pepper, oregano, 2 tsp salt and the juice of 1½ limes in a medium stock pot with water to cover. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the chicken is tender and falls off the bone, about 45 minutes.
Cool the chicken 15 minutes and lift it out. Strain the broth and save it for another use. Remove the skin and bones and dice the meat into ½-inch pieces.
Stir together the sour cream, half-and-half, the remaining ½ tsp salt, the cayenne, the juice of the last lime and the grated lime peel. Refrigerate until needed.
Heat the oven to 400°F and lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Heat about ⅛ inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Soften each tortilla a few seconds per side, then pat off the extra oil with a paper towel.
Fill each tortilla with ½ cup chicken, roll it up and set it seam side down in the pan.
Spread the lime sour cream over the top, sprinkle with the cheddar and bake 20 to 25 minutes, until heated through. Serve right away.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Poach the chicken a day ahead; the strained broth makes a ready soup base for the week.

rows.title: Honey Dijon Chicken
rows.dek: Chicken breasts browned in a skillet, then simmered in a creamy Dijon sauce sweetened with a spoon of honey. Dinner in about 25 minutes, served over herbed white and wild rice with carrots and broccoli.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 packet (about 1 oz) chicken Dijon sauce mix
1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast halves
steps: Stir the sauce mix into the milk and water and set it aside.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and sauté it 4 to 5 minutes per side.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and heat it to a boil.
Stir in the honey, cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Serve with herbed white and wild rice and a carrot and broccoli medley.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Any creamy Dijon sauce mix packet works; cook the chicken to 165°F.

rows.title: Southern Chicken Roll-Ups
rows.dek: An easy weeknight skillet: thin chicken breasts rolled around Swiss cheese, dusted in peppered flour, browned in butter, then simmered in broth with oregano. The broth cooks down into a light pan sauce to spoon over each roll.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 6 boneless skinless chicken breast halves (1½ lb)
steps: Flatten each chicken breast to ¼ inch thick.
Lay a slice of Swiss cheese on each one, roll it up jelly-roll style and hold it closed with a toothpick.
Mix the flour and pepper in a shallow bowl and roll the chicken in it to coat.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the rolls until browned, about 10 minutes, turning them often.
Add the broth and oregano and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer 12 to 14 minutes, until the juices run clear (165°F). Pull the toothpicks and spoon the pan sauce over the rolls.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Roll the cheese up tight inside the chicken so it melts in the middle instead of leaking into the pan.

rows.title: Lemon Chicken Herb Stir-Fry
rows.dek: Chicken strips stir-fried with carrot, broccoli, bamboo shoots and green onion, glazed in a lemony herb and garlic sauce with soy, then finished with mandarin oranges and sesame seeds over hot rice.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 green onions, cut into 1-inch pieces, and 1 large carrot, julienned
1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast (or boneless pork loin), cut into strips
1 cup herb and garlic marinade with lemon juice
1 Tbsp each soy sauce and sesame seeds
1 can (11 oz) mandarin orange segments, drained (optional)
steps: Heat the oil in a large wok or skillet.
Add the green onion and carrot and sauté 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, broccoli and bamboo shoots and stir-fry 7 to 9 minutes, until the chicken is no longer pink in the center.
In a small bowl, whisk the marinade, soy sauce and arrowroot together.
Add it to the wok and keep cooking, stirring constantly, until the sauce forms a glaze.
Stir in the orange segments, sprinkle with the sesame seeds, and serve over the hot rice.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Pork loin strips work the same way as the chicken.

rows.title: Nutty Chicken Dijon
rows.dek: Chicken strips and crisp stir-fry vegetables in one skillet, pulled together with a quick Dijon sauce and finished with chopped roasted peanuts. Spooned over hot rice, dinner is on the table in about half an hour.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 cups stir-fry vegetables, fresh from the produce department or frozen
1 lb boneless chicken breasts, cut into thin strips
¼ cup Dijon or country Dijon mustard
steps: Heat 2 teaspoons of the oil in an 8 to 10 inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the vegetables until tender-crisp, then remove them from the pan and keep warm.
Add the remaining oil to the same pan and cook and stir the chicken until done. Remove it from the pan and keep warm.
Blend the mustard, broth and cornstarch, and add it to the skillet.
Cook and stir over medium-high heat until the sauce thickens and boils.
Return the chicken and vegetables to the pan and heat through.
Stir in the peanuts and serve over the hot rice.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Return the stir-fry vegetables from the first step to the pan along with the chicken.

rows.title: Bacon and Double Cheese Quiche
rows.dek: A classic custard quiche: a hand-rolled butter crust baked blind, then filled with eggs, light cream and thyme, crisp bacon and two cheeses, nutty Gruyère and sharp white cheddar. Serve it warm with a tossed green salad, or freeze it for later.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Crust, 1⅓ cups all-purpose flour and ⅛ tsp salt
½ cup (1 stick) chilled butter, cut in small pieces
¼ tsp dried thyme and ⅛ tsp white pepper
½ cup shredded Gruyère cheese (about 2 oz)
½ cup shredded white cheddar cheese (about 2 oz)
steps: Mix the flour and salt, then cut in the butter with a pastry blender or 2 knives until coarse crumbs form.
Add the water a tablespoon at a time, tossing with a fork, until a dough forms. Shape a disk, wrap it and chill 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 375°F. Roll the dough to an 11-inch circle, fit it into a 9-inch pie pan, trim to a ¼-inch overhang and fold it under to a standing edge. Prick it with a fork, then line it with foil and pie weights or dried beans.
Bake 10 minutes, remove the foil and weights, and bake until lightly golden, about 5 minutes more. Cool on a wire rack.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain on a paper towel and crumble.
Whisk the eggs, cream, thyme and pepper and pour into the crust. Sprinkle with the bacon, Gruyère and cheddar.
Bake until golden and the custard is set, about 30 minutes. Serve warm with a tossed green salad.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: To freeze, cool the baked quiche completely, wrap it airtight and freeze up to 1 month.

rows.title: Chicken Piccata
rows.dek: The classic Italian-style skillet supper: thin chicken cutlets dusted in flour and browned in butter and olive oil, then finished with a quick pan sauce of lemon juice, stock, capers and parsley. Paper-thin lemon slices, sautéed for a minute, go on top.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Lightly coat the cutlets in flour and season with salt and pepper.
In a large nonstick skillet, heat 1 Tbsp butter and 1 Tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat, cook 2 cutlets until golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side (165°F inside), and move them to a plate.
Add 1 Tbsp butter and 1 Tbsp olive oil to the pan, cook the other 2 cutlets the same way, and move them to the plate.
Add the lemon slices to the pan and cook 1 minute.
Add the lemon juice and stock, scraping up the brown bits, bring to a boil and cook 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the remaining 2 Tbsp butter, the capers and the parsley, and season the sauce to taste.
Top each cutlet with 2 lemon slices and the sauce. Refrigerate any leftovers.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Brown the cutlets two at a time so they sear golden instead of steaming.

rows.title: Chicken and Black Bean Quesadillas
rows.dek: A recipe for a crowd: taco-seasoned chicken simmered with black beans, corn and salsa, folded into flour tortillas with cheese and baked until crisp. A quick homemade pico of avocado, tomato, green onion, lime and cilantro goes on the side with light sour cream.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 3 or 4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, cubed
1 (15 oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
¼ cup salsa, plus water as needed to keep it from drying
Pico de gallo: 1 medium avocado and 1 medium tomato, diced, ¼ cup chopped green onions, juice of ½ medium lime and 1 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
steps: For the pico de gallo, gently fold the avocado, tomato, green onions, lime juice and cilantro together, then cover and chill in the fridge.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, sauté the chicken until it is cooked through and no longer pink inside.
Add the taco seasoning, beans, corn, salsa and a little water to keep it from drying out. Cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Lay the tortillas on a baking sheet, top half of each with the filling, sprinkle some cheese over it and fold the tortilla over.
Bake 8 minutes, or until the tortillas are crisp.
Serve with the pico de gallo and light sour cream.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Make the pico first so it chills while the filling simmers.

rows.title: Reunion Chicken Salad
rows.dek: A family reunion favorite: chicken soaked in soy, garlic and lemon-lime soda, baked and shredded, then piled over mixed greens with mandarin oranges, green onions and crunchy chow mein noodles. A sweet, peppery creamy sesame dressing pulls it together.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 lb chicken, ¼ cup soy sauce and ¼ cup oil
Mandarin oranges and sliced green onions
Dressing: 1 cup mayo, 2 Tbsp sesame oil, 2 Tbsp lemon juice
⅓ cup sugar, ½ Tbsp ground black pepper, 5 Tbsp milk
steps: Stir the soy sauce, oil, lemon-lime soda and garlic together and marinate the chicken in it for 1 hour or longer.
Bake the chicken at 350°F for 30 minutes, or until the center reaches 165°F.
Shred the chicken.
For the dressing, whisk the mayo, sesame oil, lemon juice, sugar, pepper and milk until smooth, and chill until serving.
Fill a bowl with the salad greens and top with the chicken, mandarin oranges, green onions and chow mein noodles.
Serve with the creamy sesame dressing.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Add the chow mein noodles and dressing just before serving so the noodles stay crisp.

rows.title: Crunchy Chicken Salad
rows.dek: A make-ahead salad: chopped chicken soaks in a honey, soy, ginger and toasted sesame dressing, then goes over crisp cabbage, snow peas, carrots, green onions and radishes just before serving. Salted peanuts on top add the crunch.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ⅓ cup vegetable oil, ¼ cup vinegar, 2 Tbsp honey
2 Tbsp sesame seeds, toasted, and 2 Tbsp soy sauce
1 tsp dried parsley flakes, ½ tsp ground ginger, ½ tsp ground mustard
2 cups shredded green or Chinese cabbage
steps: In a large bowl, combine the oil, vinegar, honey, sesame seeds, soy sauce, parsley, ginger and mustard, and mix well.
Stir in the chicken, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Just before serving, toss the cabbage, snow peas, carrots, green onions and radishes in a serving bowl.
Top the vegetables with the chicken mixture.
Sprinkle with peanuts if desired, and serve.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Keep the vegetables and the dressed chicken apart until serving so the cabbage stays crisp.

rows.title: Pepper Bean Salad
rows.dek: A make-ahead bean salad: butter beans, crisp green beans, three colors of bell pepper, red onion, grape tomatoes and basil, dressed while the sweet apple vinaigrette is still hot, then chilled a full day so everything soaks it up.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Vinaigrette, 3 tbsp vinegar, 3 tbsp brown sugar and 2 tbsp olive oil
¼ tsp each salt and pepper
½ each red, green and yellow bell pepper, sliced
steps: In a heavy saucepan, combine the vinegar, brown sugar, olive oil, garlic, salt and pepper.
Simmer the vinaigrette over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Combine the green beans, onion, tomatoes, butter beans, basil and bell peppers in a bowl.
Pour the hot vinaigrette over the salad and mix thoroughly.
Cover and chill for 24 hours before serving.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Make it the day before; the long chill is what gives it its flavor.

rows.title: Spinach Salad
rows.dek: A family potluck favorite: tender spinach tossed with a buttery toasted crunch of ramen noodles, slivered almonds and sesame seeds, and a sweet soy and rice vinegar dressing. Toss it right before serving so the crunch stays crisp.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ½ cup olive oil (or grapeseed oil)
1 package ramen noodles, crushed (seasoning packet not used)
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the crushed ramen noodles, almonds and sesame seeds and stir often until golden and toasted, 6 to 8 minutes, then spread them out to cool.
Whisk the oil, sugar, rice vinegar and soy sauce until the sugar dissolves.
Just before serving, toss the spinach with the cooled crunch and as much dressing as you like.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Start with half the dressing and add more to taste.

rows.title: Piquant Pork Salad
rows.dek: A salad for a summer supper: pork tenderloin marinated in balsamic vinaigrette and grilled over indirect heat, sliced thin over mesclun with zucchini, red pepper, onion and carrots, then finished with pesto-toasted pecans and Parmesan.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ⅔ cup bottled balsamic vinaigrette salad dressing
1 medium red sweet pepper, cut into thin strips
½ small red onion, thinly sliced
½ cup peeled baby carrots, halved lengthwise
¼ cup finely shredded Parmesan cheese
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Put the pork in a plastic bag with ⅓ cup of the dressing, seal it and let it stand at room temperature 30 minutes, turning the bag now and then.
Meanwhile, toss the pecans with the pesto in a shallow baking pan and bake 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. Let them cool in the pan.
Lift the pork from the marinade and keep the marinade. In a covered grill, arrange hot coals around a drip pan and test for medium heat above the pan.

Set the pork on the rack over the drip pan with a meat thermometer in it. Grill, covered, 30 to 40 minutes, until it reads 160°F, brushing with the reserved marinade until the last 5 minutes. Discard any marinade left over.
Let the pork stand 10 minutes, then slice it thinly.
In a large salad bowl combine the mesclun, zucchini, pepper strips, onion and carrots. Add the pecans and sliced pork.
Toss with the remaining dressing and sprinkle with the Parmesan.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: No charcoal? Set a gas grill for medium indirect heat and cook the pork the same way.

rows.title: Heavenly Pineapple Mold
rows.dek: An old-fashioned molded salad: lemon gelatin made with the pineapple juice, chilled to a soft set, then folded with crushed pineapple, whipped topping and sharp cheddar. The cheese sounds odd and is the point: salty bits against the sweet, airy lemon.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 large (20-oz) can crushed pineapple, juice saved
Water, to make 2 cups with the juice
steps: Drain the pineapple and save the juice.
Add enough water to the juice to make 2 cups and bring it to a boil.
Dissolve the lemon gelatin in the boiling liquid.
Stir in the cold water and lemon juice.
Chill until the gelatin is soft set, thick but not completely set.
Fold in the pineapple first, then the whipped topping, then the grated cheese.
Spoon into a 6-cup mold or a 9x13 pan and chill until firm.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Catch the gelatin at a soft set; fully set, it won't fold smoothly.

rows.title: Orange Tapioca Salad
rows.dek: An old-fashioned fluff salad: orange gelatin and vanilla and tapioca puddings cooked together and cooled, then folded with mandarin oranges, crushed pineapple and whipped topping. A sweet, make-ahead bowl for holiday tables and potlucks.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 package (3.4 oz) instant vanilla pudding mix
1 carton (8 oz) frozen whipped topping, thawed
steps: In a saucepan, bring the water to a boil.
Whisk in the gelatin, vanilla pudding mix and tapioca pudding mix.
Return to a boil, stirring constantly, and boil for 1 minute.
Remove from the heat and cool completely.
Fold in the oranges, pineapple and whipped topping.
Spoon into a serving bowl, cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Variations: use strawberry gelatin with 2 packages (10 or 16 oz) frozen sweetened strawberries, or raspberry gelatin with 2 packages (10 or 16 oz) frozen sweetened raspberries, in place of the orange gelatin and mandarins.

rows.title: Sweet Cabbage Salad
rows.dek: A quick, crunchy cabbage salad: shredded green cabbage, sweet peas and chives softened for half an hour in a toasted sesame, apple vinegar and agave dressing, with chopped almonds tossed in right before serving.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 Tbsp light agave nectar or honey
steps: Put the cabbage, peas and chives in a large resealable plastic bag and set it aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the sesame oil, vinegar, agave nectar and salt.
Pour the dressing into the bag, seal it and toss to coat.
Let it sit for 30 minutes, shaking the bag every 10 minutes to soften the cabbage.
When ready to serve, mix in the chopped almonds.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days; after that the cabbage starts to lose its crunch.

rows.title: Thai Fruit Salad
rows.dek: A cool summer fruit salad: honeydew and watermelon chilled in a lime, brown sugar and cilantro dressing, then tossed with sliced banana just before serving and topped with dry-roasted peanuts. Sweet, tart and a little salty, with Thai flavors.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ½ tsp grated lime peel (green part only)
steps: Combine the honeydew and watermelon in a shallow casserole dish.
Stir together the lime juice, brown sugar, cilantro, lime peel and salt.
Pour the dressing over the fruit and refrigerate 1 hour.
Slice the bananas and toss them with the fruit.
Serve topped with the peanuts, if you like.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Slice the bananas only right before serving so they stay firm and bright.

rows.title: Colby Fiesta Salad
rows.dek: A taco salad baked in a pie plate: buttered flour tortillas toasted into a shell, a bed of iceberg, taco-seasoned beef with garbanzos, tomato, onion rings and olives, then a smooth Colby cheese sauce poured over the top. Cut it in wedges.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 package (1¼ oz) taco seasoning mix, plus ¾ cup water
1 can (15½ oz) garbanzo beans, rinsed and drained
1 large tomato, chopped, and 1 medium onion, sliced into rings
½ cup pitted sliced ripe olives
2 cups (8 oz) shredded Colby cheese, and chopped jalapeño peppers if desired
steps: Brush the tortillas lightly with the butter and lay them in a round pie plate, overlapping slightly. Bake at 350°F for 10 minutes.
Brown the ground chuck in a skillet until crumbly and drain off the drippings.
Add the seasoning mix and water and simmer, uncovered, 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, sprinkle the lettuce over the tortillas. Combine the beef mixture, beans, tomato, onion and olives and spoon it over the lettuce.
Heat the evaporated milk in a medium saucepan until bubbles form around the edges. Turn the heat to low and stir in the cheese until melted. Add the peppers if you like.
Pour the cheese sauce over the meat mixture. Carefully lift out the tortillas and topping and serve in wedges.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Serve it in wedges, like a pie.

rows.title: Chicken-Bean Salad
rows.dek: A cold supper salad: kidney beans and chopped chicken with celery, green onion, sweet pickles and hard-cooked egg, tossed in mayonnaise brightened with pickle juice and mustard, then spooned into crisp lettuce cups. Make it ahead and let it chill.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
2 or 3 green onions with tops, minced
½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper
1 Tbsp pickle juice and 1 tsp prepared mustard
Lettuce cups or leaves, for serving
steps: In a large bowl, combine the beans, chicken, celery, green onions, pickles and eggs.
Sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Stir the mayonnaise, pickle juice and mustard together until smooth.
Gently fold the dressing into the salad until everything is coated.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
Spoon into lettuce cups or onto lettuce leaves to serve.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Chill it at least an hour so the flavors come together.

rows.title: Summer Chickpea Salad
rows.dek: A bright, no-cook family salad: chickpeas, grape tomatoes, cucumber, green pepper, red onion and parsley tossed with lemony avocado and a simple olive oil, vinegar and cumin dressing, then chilled an hour so the flavors come together.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: ¾ cup diced green bell pepper
Dressing: ¼ cup olive oil, 2 Tbsp red vinegar, ½ tsp cumin, salt and pepper
steps: Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, cumin, salt and pepper together until well combined.
Squeeze the lemon over the cubed avocado in a large bowl and stir to coat.
Add the chickpeas, onion, tomatoes, cucumber, parsley and green pepper, pour the dressing over, and toss gently.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving.
rows.from_credit: From a family recipe card
rows.tip: Toss everything with the dressing once, gently, so the avocado stays in cubes.

rows.title: Gallo Pinto
rows.dek: Rice and beans fried together, a breakfast classic in both Costa Rica and Nicaragua. The name means "spotted rooster," for the speckled look of the beans in the rice. Finish it with a splash of Salsa Lizano.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 can black beans, with a little of their liquid
A splash of Salsa Lizano (or Worcestershire)
steps: Soften the onion and pepper in oil, about 4 minutes.
Add the beans and some of their liquid and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the rice and fry, stirring, until hot and a little crisp.
Season and stir in the cilantro.
Serve with fried or scrambled eggs, and avocado or maduros on the side.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen
rows.serve_with: Huevos a la Mexicana and Baked Maduros

rows.title: Chifrijo
rows.dek: Chifrijo is Costa Rica's favorite bar boca, named for its two stars, chicharrón and frijoles. Most accounts credit a Tibás bar owner around 1979, whose original had no rice or avocado.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp garlic powder, juice of 1 lime
2 cans (15 oz) red kidney beans, with their liquid
½ onion, ½ red bell pepper, 2 cloves garlic, minced
3 Roma tomatoes and ½ white onion, diced
½ cup cilantro, juice of 2 limes, salt
Tortilla chips, lime wedges and Salsa Lizano
steps: Toss the pork with the salt, garlic powder and lime juice.
Cover the pork with ½ cup water in a heavy pan and simmer 20 minutes, then uncover and fry in its own fat until crisp, about 25 minutes.
Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in a little oil, add the beans with their liquid and simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Mix the pico de gallo and let it sit 10 minutes.
Layer each bowl with rice, beans and chicharrón.
Top with pico de gallo and avocado, tuck chips around the edge, and serve with lime and Salsa Lizano.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen
rows.tip: Most homes add the rice and avocado.
rows.serve_with: Baked Maduros

rows.title: Arroz con Pollo
rows.dek: Chicken and rice in one pot, traditional across Spain and Latin America. Fun fact: in the Dominican Republic it's often called locrio de pollo.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 jar roasted red peppers or 1 bell pepper, chopped
2 cloves garlic and 2 tbsp tomato paste
1 tsp each cumin, paprika and oregano, 1½ tsp salt
steps: On Sauté, brown the chicken in a little oil with the salt and spices, 4–5 minutes.
Add the onion and pepper for 3 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 1.
Pour in the broth, scrape the bottom, then stir in the rice and push it under.
Cook on high pressure 10 minutes, then natural release 10 minutes.
Fluff and finish with cilantro and lime.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen
rows.serve_with: Baked Maduros and a green salad

rows.title: Pollo Guisado
rows.dek: Pollo guisado means “stewed chicken,” a home-cooking staple in Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic and Cuba. Fun fact: it appears in Puerto Rico's first cookbook, from 1859.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 tsp each cumin, oregano and paprika
1 lb yams or sweet potatoes, in chunks
steps: Season the chicken with the salt and spices and brown it on Sauté, 3 minutes a side.
Add the onion, pepper and garlic for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, broth and vinegar, scraping the bottom.
Add the yams on top and cook on high pressure 15 minutes, then natural release 10.
Finish with cilantro.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen
rows.serve_with: Baked Rice and Baked Maduros

rows.title: Picadillo
rows.dek: Picadillo comes from the Spanish picar, “to mince,” and is loved from Cuba to Mexico and Costa Rica. Fun fact: the Philippines has its own version, giniling.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 jar roasted red peppers or 1 bell pepper, chopped
3 cloves garlic or 1 tsp garlic powder
2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp each chili powder, cumin and oregano
2 tbsp tomato paste and 1 cup chicken broth
steps: Brown the beef, breaking it up, about 10 minutes, and pour off most of the fat.
Add the onion and peppers until soft, 6–8 minutes, then the garlic for 1.
Stir in the spices and tomato paste for a minute, then the broth, scraping up the browned bits.
Cover and simmer on low 20–30 minutes, then taste for salt.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen, adapted from cookprimalgourmet.com
rows.serve_with: Baked Rice, Baked Maduros and black beans

rows.title: Chicken Tinga
rows.dek: Tinga is shredded meat in a smoky chipotle-tomato sauce, presumed to come from Puebla, Mexico. Fun fact: the first known printed recipe is from 1881.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 tomatoes, chopped, and 2 tbsp tomato paste
1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp oregano, ½ tsp salt
steps: Sauté the onion and garlic in a little oil, 3–4 minutes, then scrape the bottom with a splash of broth.
Blend the rest of the broth with the tomato paste, tomatoes, chipotles, adobo and spices.
Add the chicken and sauce and cook on high pressure 9 minutes, then quick release.
Shred the chicken in the sauce and serve in tacos or bowls.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen, adapted from wholesomelicious.com
rows.serve_with: Guacamole and refried beans

rows.title: Peruvian Chicken with Ají Verde
rows.dek: An oven take on pollo a la brasa, Peru's rotisserie chicken, first roasted near Lima around 1950. Fun fact: the first versions used only salt.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 tbsp oil, 2 tbsp vinegar, juice of 1 lime
3 cloves garlic, 1 tsp each cumin, paprika and salt
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp chipotle adobo
¾ cup mayonnaise, juice of 1 lime, 1 jalapeño, cilantro, 1 clove garlic, salt
steps: Marinate the chicken 4 hours or overnight.
Blend the ají verde until smooth.
Roast skin up at 425°F about 45 minutes, to 165°F, then broil 2–3 minutes and rest 5.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen, adapted from cookprimalgourmet.com
rows.serve_with: Roasted yams and green beans

rows.title: Huevos a la Mexicana
rows.dek: Huevos a la mexicana are Mexico's everyday scrambled eggs, cooked with tomato, white onion and green chile. Fun fact: the dish is named for those three colors, red, white and green, the colors of the Mexican flag.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 tomato or a handful of cherry tomatoes, diced
Warm tortillas, black beans and cheese, to serve
steps: Soften the onion and jalapeño in oil, 2 minutes.
Add the tomato for 1 minute.
Pour in the beaten eggs with salt and scramble softly.
Top with cilantro.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen
rows.tip: Rancheros style, put fried eggs on tortillas with beans, cheese and salsa.
rows.serve_with: Refried beans and Guacamole

rows.title: Tuna Ceviche Bowl
rows.dek: Ceviche, raw fish "cooked" in citrus juice, is Peru's national dish, declared part of its national heritage in 2004 and recognized by UNESCO in 2023. This quick bowl uses canned tuna instead. Fun fact: Peru celebrates National Ceviche Day every June 28.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Cilantro, a little jalapeño and salt
steps: Mix everything but the avocado.
Let it sit 2 minutes.
Top with the avocado.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen
rows.serve_with: Tostadas and a green salad

rows.title: Baked Maduros
rows.dek: Maduros are ripe plantains cooked until sweet and caramelized, a side loved across the Caribbean and Latin America and especially tied to Cuba. Plantains first came from Southeast Asia. Fun fact: maduro means "mature" in Spanish, for the fully ripe, nearly black fruit.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Peel the plantains and cut them on a diagonal into ½-inch slices.
Toss with the oil and salt and spread on a lined pan.
Bake 20–25 minutes, flipping once, until caramelized.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen, adapted from diabetesfoodhub.org
rows.tip: Let the plantains ripen on the counter until the skins are mostly black.
rows.serve_with: Picadillo or Gallo Pinto

rows.title: Baja Shrimp Tacos with Chipotle Crema
rows.dek: Baja-style tacos are traditionally traced to the fish stands of Ensenada in the late 1950s. Fun fact: Ensenada's oldest surviving fish taco stand opened in 1970.
rows.image_alt: Baja Shrimp Tacos with Chipotle Crema
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 tsp chili powder, ½ tsp cumin, garlic powder and salt
½ cup Greek yogurt or sour cream
1 chipotle, 1 tsp adobo, juice of ½ lime, salt
Tortillas, shredded cabbage, cilantro, lime and avocado
steps: Stir the crema together and toss the cabbage with lime, cilantro and salt.
Pat the shrimp dry, season it and brown it in a hot pan with a little oil, 2–3 minutes.
Fill the tortillas with slaw, shrimp, crema and avocado.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen, adapted from momskitchenhandbook.com
rows.serve_with: Guacamole and Mexican rice

rows.title: Guacamole
rows.dek: Guacamole was already part of Aztec cooking when the Spanish arrived, and its name comes from the Nahuatl ahuacamolli, "avocado sauce." Onion, cilantro and lime came later.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Mix the shallot, lime juice and salt and let it sit 10 minutes.
Mash half the avocado with a fork and stir in the shallot mix.
Cut the rest into ¾-inch cubes and fold them in gently.
Season with pepper and chile powder to taste.
Eat right away.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen, adapted from Nom Nom Paleo
rows.serve_with: Taco Pie, Chicken Tinga or tortilla chips

rows.title: Dry-Brined Roast Turkey
rows.dek: Roast turkey became the heart of the American Thanksgiving table in the 1800s, and the holiday went national in 1863. Fun fact: turkey probably wasn't served at the 1621 harvest feast.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: The night before, remove the giblets, pat dry, rub with the salt, seasoning and pepper, and refrigerate uncovered.
Let it sit out 30 minutes while the oven heats to 325°F.
Brush with butter and set it breast up on a rack in the roaster, with the broth in the pan.
Roast about 3–3½ hours, to 165°F in the thickest part. Tent with foil if it browns early.
Rest 30 minutes, then carve. Save the pan juices for the gravy.
rows.from_credit: From a family holiday table
rows.serve_with: Turkey Gravy, Homemade Cranberry Sauce and Sweet Potato Casserole

rows.title: Turkey Gravy
rows.dek: Pan gravy, drippings thickened with butter and flour, has been on English tables for centuries. Smooth, savory and made right in the roasting pan.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: Broth, to make 4 cups with the drippings
steps: Skim the fat off the drippings.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Slowly whisk in the drippings plus broth to make 4 cups.
Simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Season with salt and pepper.
rows.from_credit: From a family holiday table
rows.tip: To make it ahead, refrigerate it and reheat on low, whisking in a splash of broth.
rows.serve_with: Dry-Brined Roast Turkey and mashed potatoes

rows.title: Homemade Cranberry Sauce
rows.dek: Cranberries are native to North America, and cranberry sauce has long been a Thanksgiving side. Fun fact: a Massachusetts cranberry grower first canned the sauce in 1912, and the jellied log in a can went nationwide in 1941.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
steps: Bring the sugar, water and orange juice to a boil.
Add the cranberries and simmer about 10 minutes, until most have popped.
Stir in the zest.
Cool, then refrigerate covered in a serving bowl.
rows.from_credit: From a family holiday table
rows.tip: It looks loose but sets as it cools.
rows.serve_with: Dry-Brined Roast Turkey

rows.title: Sweet Potato Casserole
rows.dek: Sweet potatoes under browned marshmallows, a Thanksgiving classic that began as a 1917 marshmallow company recipe. Sweet, soft and gone fast.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 5 lb sweet potatoes, peeled and chunked
steps: Cook the sweet potatoes and yams in the Instant Pot with 1 cup water, high pressure 8 minutes, then quick release.
Mash with the butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Spread in a 9×13 pan. It can be covered and refrigerated a day ahead.
Bake uncovered at 350°F for 30 minutes.
Add the marshmallows for the last 10 minutes.
rows.from_credit: From a family holiday table
rows.serve_with: Dry-Brined Roast Turkey and Turkey Gravy

rows.title: Polpette di Vitello
rows.dek: Polpette are small Italian meatballs, here made with veal. Fun fact: this version mixes in mashed garlic cauliflower where classic recipes use milk-soaked bread, so they stay tender without grain or dairy. Adapted from Nom Nom Paleo.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 lb ground veal, or ground beef
½ cup minced basil and ½ cup minced parsley
2 tsp kosher salt, 1 tsp black pepper
½ yellow onion, minced fine, and 2 cloves garlic, minced
steps: Mix everything except the ghee and marinara gently by hand.
Roll the mix into 1½-inch balls.
Heat the ghee in a large skillet over medium-high until it shimmers, coming halfway up the meatballs.
Fry in batches, turning, about 2 minutes until cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack and serve plain or with marinara.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen, adapted from Nom Nom Paleo
rows.tip: Freeze extras on a sheet pan, then bag them for quick lunches.

rows.title: Green Chicken
rows.dek: A paleo, Thai-style herb marinade turns plain chicken bright green and tangy. Fun fact: the marinade keeps in the freezer, so a double batch saves a later week. Adapted from Nom Nom Paleo.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 sweet onion, 1¼ cups basil, 1 cup cilantro, ¼ cup mint
3 cloves garlic, ¼ cup paleo fish sauce, 2 Tbsp apple juice
1 tsp Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, ½ tsp black pepper, zest of 1 lime
3 lb skin-on chicken thighs or drumsticks
steps: Blend all the marinade ingredients until smooth.
Seal the chicken in a gallon bag with the marinade and refrigerate 1 hour to 1 day.
Take it out 30 minutes before cooking.
Roast on a rack over a foil-lined sheet at 400°F for 35–40 minutes, flipping halfway, or grill over medium-hot heat about 25 minutes.
It's done at 170°F inside; serve with lime wedges.
rows.from_credit: From our kitchen, adapted from Nom Nom Paleo
rows.tip: Freeze half the marinade flat in a bag for a later week.

rows.title: Pollo Delicia
rows.dek: Una favorita de la familia, un horneado agridulce de la cocina estadounidense de productos listos, donde una botella y un sobre se encargaban de sazonar. Fácil y con mucho sabor.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 pollo entero, en piezas (pechugas, piernas y muslos)
½ botella de aderezo Catalina (aderezo dulce de tomate), unos 240 ml (8 oz)
1 sobre de sopa de cebolla deshidratada
1 frasco pequeño de mermelada de albaricoque (chabacano)
steps: Coloque el pollo en un refractario.
Mezcle el aderezo, la sopa de cebolla y la mermelada.
Vierta la salsa sobre el pollo.
Hornee 1 hora a 175 °C (350 °F).
Sirva con arroz y bañe el arroz con la salsa que sobre.
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar
rows.tip: Si no hay de albaricoque, la mermelada de frambuesa también funciona.
rows.serve_with: Arroz al horno y ejotes al vapor

rows.title: Pollo que se deshace en la boca
rows.dek: Una favorita de la familia: pollo horneado con una costra de mayonesa y parmesano, como el que Hellmann's publica como su Parmesan Crusted Chicken. Queda jugoso y dorado.
rows.image_alt: Pollo que se deshace en la boca
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 50 g (½ taza) de queso parmesano rallado
steps: Mezcle el parmesano, la mayonesa y los condimentos.
Unte la mezcla sobre las pechugas.
Hornee 45 minutos a 190 °C (375 °F).
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar
rows.serve_with: Arroz al horno y brócoli al vapor

rows.title: Pollo crujiente al horno, fácil
rows.dek: Una favorita de la familia, la versión casera del pollo frito sureño: se pasa por harina sazonada y se hornea con mantequilla en lugar de freírlo en mucha grasa.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2–3 muslos de pollo y 2 pechugas partidas por la mitad
steps: Derrita la mantequilla en un molde poco profundo dentro del horno a 200 °C (400 °F).
Mezcle la harina sazonada y pase el pollo por ella.
Acomode el pollo en el molde en una sola capa, con la piel hacia abajo.
Hornee 30 minutos y luego voltéelo.
Hornee hasta que esté tierno, unos 30 minutos más.
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar
rows.serve_with: Puré de papas y ejotes

rows.title: Pollo con arroz: ¡fácil!
rows.dek: Una favorita de la familia: un plato de “echar todo y hornear” de la tradición estadounidense de guisos con sopa condensada de lata y un sobre de sopa de cebolla. Todo va en un solo molde.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 lata de crema de pollo condensada
1 sobre de sopa de cebolla deshidratada
Unas 3 pechugas de pollo sin hueso
steps: Mezcle la crema de pollo, el agua y la sopa de cebolla.
Incorpore el arroz con un tenedor.
Coloque el pollo en el fondo de un molde de 23 × 33 cm (9 × 13 pulg.).
Vierta la mezcla de arroz sobre el pollo.
Tape con papel aluminio y hornee 1 hora a 175 °C (350 °F).
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar
rows.serve_with: Ejotes al vapor y una ensalada verde

rows.title: Pollo con brócoli
rows.dek: Una favorita de la familia, versión casera del chicken divan, aquel plato de un hotel de Nueva York. En las casas se cambió su salsa cremosa por sopa de lata y mayonesa.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 2 paquetes de 285 g (10 oz) de brócoli congelado, o fresco
1 lata de crema de pollo condensada
60 g (½ taza) de queso cheddar añejo rallado
steps: Cueza el pollo a fuego lento 20 minutos; luego quítele los huesos y la piel y córtelo en trozos del tamaño de un bocado.
Cocine el brócoli 4 minutos; debe quedar crujiente.
Acomode el brócoli a lo largo en un refractario poco profundo y extienda el pollo encima.
Mezcle la crema de pollo, la mayonesa, el jugo de limón y el curry, y viértalo sobre el pollo.
Espolvoree el queso por encima y después el pan molido.
Hornee 30 minutos a 175 °C (350 °F).
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar
rows.serve_with: Arroz al horno y una ensalada verde

rows.title: Arroz al horno
rows.dek: Una favorita de la familia: arroz que se cocina suavemente en un recipiente tapado dentro del horno, sin ninguna olla que vigilar. Suelto, sabroso y rinde para muchos.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 300 g (1½ tazas) de arroz blanco común, crudo
steps: Use un refractario de 1,5 litros (1½ cuartos de galón) sin engrasar, con una tapa que cierre bien (o papel aluminio).
Ponga todo adentro y tápelo.
Hornee 45 minutos a 190 °C (375 °F). No destape ni revuelva.
Esponje el arroz con un tenedor al servir.
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar
rows.serve_with: Pollo Delicia o Pollo guisado

rows.title: Pastel de taco
rows.dek: Una favorita de la familia, un guiso al horno tex-mex armado sobre masa refrigerada para cuernitos. El relleno de taco, los Fritos y el queso se hornean en un pastel que se corta en rebanadas.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) de carne molida de res
1 lata de granos de elote, escurridos
1 paquete de masa refrigerada para cuernitos (crescent rolls)
240–480 ml (1–2 tazas) de Fritos (chips de maíz) triturados
Aguacate fresco y salsa, para servir
steps: Dore la carne y escúrrale la grasa.
Agregue el sazonador y el agua y cocine a fuego lento 5 minutos.
Incorpore el elote y las aceitunas.
Presione la masa en un molde para pay sin engrasar para formar la base.
Espolvoree la mitad de los Fritos sobre la base.
Haga capas de carne, crema agria y queso, y termine con el resto de los Fritos.
Hornee 25 minutos a 190 °C (375 °F).
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar
rows.serve_with: Guacamole, arroz a la mexicana y frijoles refritos
rows.pairs_with: Coca-Cola mexicana o agua de jamaica

rows.title: Pasta de garbanzo para sándwiches
rows.dek: Una pasta para sándwiches hecha de garbanzo, uno de los cultivos más antiguos del mundo. Cremosa, sencilla y deliciosa en pan o con verduras.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 1 lata de 440 g (15½ oz) de garbanzos, escurridos y picados
80 ml (⅓ taza) de cebolla verde (cebollín) picada
360 ml (1½ tazas) de germinados de alfalfa
steps: Mezcle todo excepto los germinados.
Sirva con los germinados en pan de centeno, pan pita o pan de masa madre tostado.
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar
rows.serve_with: Fruta fresca y una ensalada verde

rows.title: Ponche caliente de cítricos
rows.dek: Un ponche caliente y especiado de cítricos para las fiestas. Se cuece a fuego suave, perfuma toda la casa y se mantiene tibio durante la reunión.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 480 ml (2 tazas) de jugo de naranja
180 ml (¾ taza) de jugo de limón
1,9 litros (2 cuartos de galón) de agua
steps: Hierva los 480 ml (2 tazas) de agua con el azúcar durante 5 minutos.
Agregue el resto de los ingredientes y deje que suelte el hervor.
Baje el fuego y cocine a fuego lento 30 minutos.
Retire las rajas de canela y los clavos antes de servir.
rows.from_credit: De una tarjeta de recetas familiar

rows.title: Gallo pinto
rows.dek: Arroz y frijoles fritos juntos, un clásico del desayuno en Costa Rica y Nicaragua. El nombre alude al aspecto moteado de los frijoles, como un gallo pinto. Termínelo con un chorrito de Salsa Lizano.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 320–480 g (2–3 tazas) de arroz cocido (mejor si es del día anterior)
1 lata de frijoles negros, con un poco de su líquido
Un chorrito de Salsa Lizano (o salsa inglesa Worcestershire)
steps: Sofría la cebolla y el pimiento en aceite hasta que se ablanden, unos 4 minutos.
Agregue los frijoles con parte de su líquido y cocine a fuego lento 2 minutos.
Agregue el arroz y fríalo, revolviendo, hasta que esté caliente y un poco crujiente.
Sazone e incorpore el cilantro.
Sirva con huevos fritos o revueltos, y aguacate o maduros al lado.
rows.from_credit: De nuestra cocina
rows.serve_with: Huevos a la mexicana y Maduros al horno

rows.title: Chifrijo
rows.dek: El chifrijo es la botana favorita de Costa Rica, y su nombre une a sus dos estrellas: el chicharrón y los frijoles. Se sirve en capas, con arroz, pico de gallo y limón.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 700 g (1½ lb) de panceta de cerdo, en cubos de 2,5 cm (1 pulg.)
1 cdta de sal, ½ cdta de ajo en polvo y el jugo de 1 limón
2 latas de 425 g (15 oz) de frijoles rojos, con su líquido
½ cebolla, ½ pimiento rojo y 2 dientes de ajo, picados finamente
480 g (3 tazas) de arroz blanco cocido
3 tomates roma y ½ cebolla blanca, en cubitos
120 ml (½ taza) de cilantro, el jugo de 2 limones y sal
Totopos (chips de tortilla), gajos de limón y Salsa Lizano
steps: Mezcle el cerdo con la sal, el ajo en polvo y el jugo de limón.
Ponga el cerdo en una olla de fondo grueso, cúbralo con 120 ml (½ taza) de agua y cocine a fuego lento 20 minutos; luego destape y fríalo en su propia grasa hasta que esté crujiente, unos 25 minutos.
Sofría la cebolla, el pimiento y el ajo en un poco de aceite, agregue los frijoles con su líquido y cocine a fuego lento 15 minutos, hasta que espesen.
Mezcle el pico de gallo y déjelo reposar 10 minutos.
En cada tazón, haga capas de arroz, frijoles y chicharrón.
Corone con pico de gallo y aguacate, acomode los totopos alrededor del borde y sirva con limón y Salsa Lizano.
rows.from_credit: De nuestra cocina
rows.tip: La versión original no lleva arroz ni aguacate; en la mayoría de las casas se le agregan ambos.
rows.serve_with: Maduros al horno

rows.title: Arroz con pollo
rows.dek: Pollo y arroz en una sola olla, un plato tradicional en España y en toda América Latina. Dato curioso: en la República Dominicana a menudo se le llama locrio de pollo.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) de muslos de pollo, en trozos
1 frasco de pimientos rojos asados o 1 pimiento, picado
2 dientes de ajo y 2 cda de pasta de tomate
1 cdta de comino, 1 de paprika y 1 de orégano; 1½ cdta de sal
300 g (1½ tazas) de arroz blanco, enjuagado
420 ml (1¾ tazas) de caldo de pollo
steps: En la función Sauté (saltear), dore el pollo en un poco de aceite con la sal y las especias, 4–5 minutos.
Agregue la cebolla y el pimiento por 3 minutos, y luego el ajo y la pasta de tomate por 1 minuto.
Vierta el caldo, raspe el fondo y luego incorpore el arroz, hundiéndolo en el líquido.
Cocine a presión alta 10 minutos y deje que la presión se libere de forma natural durante 10 minutos.
Esponje el arroz y termine con cilantro y limón.
rows.from_credit: De nuestra cocina
rows.serve_with: Maduros al horno y una ensalada verde

rows.title: Pollo guisado
rows.dek: El pollo guisado, pollo cocido despacio en su propia salsa, es un básico de la cocina casera en Puerto Rico, la República Dominicana y Cuba. Dato curioso: aparece en el primer libro de cocina de Puerto Rico, de 1859.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 4 cuartos de pollo (pierna con muslo), sin piel
3 dientes de ajo o ajo en polvo
240 ml (1 taza) de caldo y 1 cda de vinagre
1 cdta de comino, 1 de orégano y 1 de paprika
450 g (1 lb) de ñame o camote, en trozos
steps: Sazone el pollo con la sal y las especias y dórelo en la función Sauté, 3 minutos por lado.
Agregue la cebolla, el pimiento y el ajo por 2 minutos.
Incorpore la pasta de tomate, el caldo y el vinagre, raspando el fondo.
Ponga el ñame encima y cocine a presión alta 15 minutos; luego deje que la presión se libere de forma natural durante 10.
Termine con cilantro.
rows.from_credit: De nuestra cocina
rows.serve_with: Arroz al horno y Maduros al horno

rows.title: Picadillo
rows.dek: El picadillo debe su nombre al verbo picar y se disfruta desde Cuba hasta México y Costa Rica. Dato curioso: Filipinas tiene su propia versión, el giniling.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) de carne molida de res
1 frasco de pimientos rojos asados o 1 pimiento morrón, picado
3 dientes de ajo o 1 cdta de ajo en polvo
2 cdta de pimentón (paprika) y 1 cdta de cada uno: chile en polvo, comino y orégano
2 cda de pasta de tomate y 240 ml (1 taza) de caldo de pollo
steps: Dore la carne desmenuzándola, unos 10 minutos, y retire casi toda la grasa.
Agregue la cebolla y los pimientos y cocine hasta que se ablanden, 6–8 minutos; luego el ajo, 1 minuto más.
Incorpore las especias y la pasta de tomate por un minuto; luego el caldo, raspando los trocitos dorados del fondo.
Tape y cocine a fuego bajo 20–30 minutos; pruebe y ajuste la sal.
rows.from_credit: De nuestra cocina, adaptada de cookprimalgourmet.com
rows.serve_with: Arroz al horno, Maduros al horno y frijoles negros

rows.title: Tinga de pollo
rows.dek: La tinga es carne deshebrada en una salsa ahumada de chipotle y tomate, que se cree originaria de Puebla, México. Dato curioso: la primera receta impresa que se conoce es de 1881.
rows.image_license: Generated for this recipe book with Higgsfield
ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) de muslos de pollo
1 cebolla en rodajas y 2–3 dientes de ajo
2 tomates picados y 2 cda de pasta de tomate
2 chiles chipotles y 1 cda de adobo
1 cdta de comino, ½ cdta de orégano, ½ cdta de sal
160 ml (⅔ taza) de caldo de pollo
steps: Sofría la cebolla y el ajo en un poco de aceite, 3–4 minutos; luego raspe el fondo con un chorrito de caldo.
Licúe el resto del caldo con la pasta de tomate, los tomates, los chipotles, el adobo y las especias.
Agregue el pollo y la salsa y cocine a presión alta 9 minutos; luego libere la presión rápidamente.
Deshebre el pollo en la salsa y sírvalo en tacos o en bowls.
rows.from_credit: De nuestra cocina, adaptada de wholesomelicious.com
rows.serve_with: Guacamole y frijoles refritos

rows.title: Pollo a la peruana con ají verde
rows.dek: Una versión al horno del pollo a la brasa, el pollo rostizado del Perú, que se asó por primera vez cerca de Lima hacia 1950. Dato curioso: las primeras versiones solo llevaban sal.
